Яка різниця у віці ідеальна для стосунків
  - Author, Олеся Жигалюк
  - Role, ВВС News Україна
- Published
- Час прочитання: 6 хв
Різниця у віці між партнерами давно викликає суперечки. Одні вважають, що такі стосунки приречені. Інші переконані: якщо люди люблять одне одного, вік не має значення.
Але чи справді пари з великою різницею у віці частіше розлучаються? Чи впливає вік партнерів на сексуальне життя, доходи та тривалість життя?
Psychology Today і Economist проаналізували дослідження, які допомагають відповісти на ці запитання.
Чому чоловіків приваблюють молодші жінки
Еволюційна психологія пояснює це традиційними уявленнями про чоловічі й жіночі ролі.
Історично жінки могли віддавати перевагу чоловікам з матеріальними ресурсами та життєвим досвідом, а чоловіків приваблювали молодість і енергія партнерок.
Однак сучасні стосунки вже не так залежать від цих уявлень.
На іншу закономірність звертає увагу Economist. Видання аналізує дослідження Кристіана Раддера, співзасновника сайту знайомств OKCupid.
Хоч це і не соціологічне дослідження, але, за його даними, жінки частіше обирають чоловіків приблизно свого віку або трохи старших. Чоловіки ж, незалежно від власного віку, віддають перевагу 20-річним жінкам.
Журналістка Сумая Кейнс також нагадує про популярне правило "половина свого віку плюс сім", за яким визначають мінімальний прийнятний вік партнера.
Наприклад, для 38-річної людини за цією формулою мінімальний вік партнера чи партнерки становить 26 років, для 50-річної - 32.
Однак це лише умовна формула, а не наукове правило.
Молодший партнер - краще сексуальне життя?
Psychology Today наводить дослідження 2025 року.
Воно показало, що в окремих групах старших людей, які зустрічалися з молодшими партнерами, рівень сексуального та загального задоволення був вищим.
Проте результати залежали від статі та віку учасників.
Старші чоловіки, які зустрічалися з молодшими жінками, частіше переживали через свої сексуальні можливості, ніж молодші чоловіки зі старшими партнерками.
Молоді жінки, які були у стосунках зі старшими чоловіками, розповідали про нижчий рівень сексуального задоволення, збудження та частоти оргазмів, ніж старші жінки з молодшими партнерами.
Але це не означає, що всі в таких парах були автоматично задоволені чи не задоволені сексуальним життям.
Важливі також фізичне здоров'я, взаємне бажання, емоційна близькість і те, наскільки комфортно людям разом.
Чи впливає вік партнера на кар'єру і доходи?
Оскільки доходи зазвичай зростають із віком, а жінки нерідко обирають старших чоловіків, у родині може бути помітна різниця в заробітках.
Особливо це відчутно після народження дітей. Якщо чоловік заробляє більше, жінці може бути легше залишити роботу або скоротити робочий час.
Але це також може позначитися на її кар'єрі та фінансовій незалежності.
Економісти припускали, що шлюби між людьми приблизно одного віку могли б допомогти зменшити гендерний розрив у доходах.
Однак дослідження, на яке посилається Economist, не підтвердило цієї гіпотези.
Доходи жінок, які вийшли заміж за старших чоловіків, у середньому не відрізнялися від доходів тих, хто обрав партнерів приблизно свого віку.
Отже, сама різниця у віці не визначає, скільки зароблятиме жінка. Важливіше те, як у сім'ї розподіляють роботу, догляд за дітьми та фінансову відповідальність.
Велика різниця у віці - більше розлучень?
У 2014 році видання Atlantic писало, що різниця у віці в п'ять років пов'язана із підвищенням імовірності розлучення на 18% порівняно з парами приблизно одного віку.
Але тут важливо розрізняти статистичний зв'язок і причину. Дослідження показало певну закономірність, проте не довело, що саме різниця у віці призводить до розлучення.
Британське Управління національної статистики також не виявило сильного зв'язку між віком подружжя та розлученнями в Англії й Уельсі.
Водночас деякі закономірності все ж простежувалися.
Жінки, які після 30 років виходили заміж за чоловіків, молодших більш ніж на 10 років, частіше розлучалися. Однак ці дані не дозволяють стверджувати, що причиною була саме різниця у віці.

Якщо ці плани не збігаються, партнерам доведеться шукати компроміси. І саме тут різниця у віці може стати джерелом конфліктів.
Молода дружина - запорука довголіття?
Economist наводить дослідження Свена Дрефаля зі Стокгольмського університету, присвячене людям старше 50 років у Данії.
За його результатами, чоловіки, одружені з молодшими жінками, жили довше, ніж ті, чиї дружини були приблизно їхнього віку.
Проте дослідження не довело, що саме молодша партнерка продовжує життя чоловіка. Можливо, здоровіші чоловіки частіше приваблюють молодших жінок і водночас мають більше шансів прожити довше.
Для жінок результати були іншими. Що більшою була різниця у віці з партнером, то меншою була ймовірність, що жінка проживе довше. І це не залежало від того, була вона старшою чи молодшою за чоловіка.

title: New wave of bomb threats hit European airlines
content_c:
New wave of bomb threats hit European airlines
- Published
European airlines have again been hit with a new wave of bomb threats - in the third such incident this week.
On Friday multiple flights to and from Lisbon, Rome, Prague and Sofia were targeted and the threats saw three planes escorted by Hungarian fighter jets, authorities said.
It also saw a number of high-profile media organisations, including Ireland's public broadcaster RTÉ, evacuated after threats were made against them - although there has been no concrete links between the messages against airlines and the broadcasters.
The disruption comes after nearly 30 aircraft and several airports across Europe were impacted by threats earlier this week, in what the UK called a "malicious hoax".
- Russian extremist group denies sending hoax bomb threats 
  - Published17 hours ago
A Ryanair flight scheduled to leave Lisbon for Rome on Friday was targeted with a threat, the airline said, while at least 11 flights were targeted in the Czech Republic and Bulgaria, according to AFP.
France also reported at least four of its flights were targeted by threats, however they all landed safely.
No explosives have been found on any planes as of Friday.
As airlines were dealing with this latest wave of threats, several media outlets, including RTÉ, were evacuated after similar warnings were made against them.
Staff at the Irish Independent newspaper and the Dublin offices of radio stations NewstalkFM and TodayFM, were also advised to leave their buildings and UK broadcaster Sky said it also received a security threat.
In a statement, gardaí (Irish police) said they were "aware of a threat made against media organisations here and in Europe".
While no link has been established between the threats against airlines and media outlets, the Irish government has warned it is a "likely coordinated campaign of disruption".
In a statement, it said: "Hoax threats such as these cause fear, distress and disruption to people going about their daily lives and activities; they achieve no positive purpose whatsoever. It is not known yet who is responsible for these threats, whether it is individuals or a centralised or co-ordinated effort.
Irish Prime Minister Micheál Martin described the situation as "worrying" and added his government's first priority was the safety of the Irish public.
"Yesterday, there appeared to be coordinated efforts to disrupt air travel," he said.
Martin told RTÉ it was not yet known if the threats had come from individuals or if it was a "coordinated attack" but said they were being taken seriously.
Ireland is scheduled to host two high-profile European Union meetings in Dublin next week.
Broadcaster Sky confirmed it had received a security threat, hours after RTÉ had evacuated its building.
The broadcaster, which is owned by Comcast, said in a statement read by a presenter on its news channel that the broadcaster had "carried out a security assessment and reported the matter to the relevant authorities".
"The safety and security of our colleagues is our primary concern, and we are working closely with authorities to ensure our people and operations remain secure."
Friday's disruption comes after the Russian extremist group "Male State", named in this week's hoax bomb threats to Italian airports, denied any link to the false warnings.

New wave of bomb threats hit European airlines
- Published
European airlines have again been hit with a new wave of bomb threats - in the third such incident this week.
On Friday multiple flights to and from Lisbon, Rome, Prague and Sofia were targeted and the threats saw three planes escorted by Hungarian fighter jets, authorities said.
It also saw a number of high-profile media organisations, including Ireland's public broadcaster RTÉ, evacuated after threats were made against them - although there has been no concrete links between the messages against airlines and the broadcasters.
The disruption comes after nearly 30 aircraft and several airports across Europe were impacted by threats earlier this week, in what the UK called a "malicious hoax".
- Russian extremist group denies sending hoax bomb threats 
  - Published17 hours ago
A Ryanair flight scheduled to leave Lisbon for Rome on Friday was targeted with a threat, the airline said, while at least 11 flights were targeted in the Czech Republic and Bulgaria, according to AFP.
France also reported at least four of its flights were targeted by threats, however they all landed safely.
No explosives have been found on any planes as of Friday.
As airlines were dealing with this latest wave of threats, several media outlets, including RTÉ, were evacuated after similar warnings were made against them.
Staff at the Irish Independent newspaper and the Dublin offices of radio stations NewstalkFM and TodayFM, were also advised to leave their buildings and UK broadcaster Sky said it also received a security threat.
In a statement, gardaí (Irish police) said they were "aware of a threat made against media organisations here and in Europe".
While no link has been established between the threats against airlines and media outlets, the Irish government has warned it is a "likely coordinated campaign of disruption".
In a statement, it said: "Hoax threats such as these cause fear, distress and disruption to people going about their daily lives and activities; they achieve no positive purpose whatsoever. title: Why smoky bacon crisps threaten to reignite rows over EU rules
content_c:
Why smoky bacon crisps threaten to reignite rows over EU rules
- Published
The naming of smoky bacon-flavoured crisps has become the latest political headache to emerge from the government's bid for closer ties with the EU.
The government is negotiating a deal on food standards in a bid to cut costs for British companies trading with Europe.
Labour ministers have been keen to talk up the potential economic benefits of the agreement, which could be announced at a summit later this month.
But the deal's requirement for Britain to adopt EU food rules in a wide range of areas has threatened to reignite sovereignty debates from the Brexit era.
Labour ministers have been keen to sidestep talking about the impact of alignment in particular sectors, instead stressing the overall economic boost it expects the food deal to bring.
On Thursday, Environment Secretary Angela Eagle told a radio presenter he should "get a life" when he asked about the potential impact of the new rules on snacks, such as smoky bacon crisps.
But it highlights the political dangers for the government of realigning with regulations that British politicians have not been able to shape, with the Conservatives and Reform UK keen to pounce on cases showing Britain to be a "rule taker" from Brussels.
It is not the first regulatory skirmish over smoky bacon crisps - following previous headlines over how the well-loved British flavour could be affected by an EU decision in 2024 to phase out a number of artificial smoke flavourings.
Now, the flavour name itself has been called into question by a separate EU attempt to restrict how descriptions of meat are used to market food.
Under rules adopted this summer, the EU plans to restrict the use of 31 terms, including bacon, drumstick and steak, to products that contain meat, claiming consumers could be confused by plant-based alternatives using the same names.
The European snack industry is seeking clarity on how the rules, which will also cover terms such as pork, chicken and beef, would apply to meat-flavoured crisps, including those flavoured without the use of any meat extracts.
The UK government has said it expects the new regulations to be in scope of its proposed food standards deal.
This means they would also apply to companies marketing their products in Britain, which is among the biggest consumers of crisps in Europe, according to analysts Euromonitor., external
Uncertainty over rules
It has raised the prospect that crisps with names such as smoky bacon and roast chicken could have to be relabelled to be sold in British shops, although much remains unclear about how the rules will apply in practice.
The new EU rules, which will not come into force until after August 2029, will allow the European Commission to create exemptions for meaty names with an established long-term use to describe other types of food product.
The Brussels-based body is yet to set out how it plans to use this power, or what it means for snacks.
A group of conservative German MEPs are also seeking a specific carve-out for meat names in snacks and sauces in separate legislation, external currently making its way through the European Parliament.
The Food and Drink Federation, which represents British crispmakers including Walkers and KP Snacks, has been supportive of the government's bid to reach a food deal due to its potential to reduce trade barriers with Europe.
But it has highlighted the new rules as an example of where it wants the government to work with industry to ensure UK interests are reflected in EU decision making.
"Meat protections are an example of a new EU rule that UK businesses will need to comply with, but which the UK was not involved in developing," added the body's chief scientific officer Kate Halliwell.
'Unintended consequences'
The Potato Processors' Association, which also represents a number of major snackmakers, said it was monitoring the situation closely and wanted to see clarification of how the rules could affect its members.
Vanessa Richardson, its deputy director general, said her association supported moves to reduce "unnecessary barriers" in the trade of food products.
But she added it was important that the government's deal is implemented in a way that "avoids unintended consequences for established product descriptions which consumers clearly understand as referring to a flavour".
The Department for Environment, Food & Rural Affairs (Defra) says it stands ready to help British snack businesses prepare for the impact of the new EU rules.
It is not yet clear what a British version of the rules would look like, or whether they would need to apply from 2029 alongside the new European regulations.

title: Food bank to close amid rising costs
content_c:
Food bank to close amid rising costs
- Published
A food bank serving an East Yorkshire town has closed after 16 years due to rising costs and a drop in donations.
The Mission Trinity Food Bank, which supports people in Goole and the surrounding villages, began as part of the local Methodist church's mission to help homeless people and those facing financial hardship.
Founder David Sample said: "Over time our funds have declined and declined, to the point where we can't really afford to keep going much longer, and also because of this cost of living crisis that's going on at the moment."
He said the charity was buying in food up to three times a week to keep up with demand despite a drop in donations.
"We've had to go out and buy more food with our funds, so we've been spending an awful lot more just to keep the basics in," he said.
He said personal circumstances had also incluenced the decision.
Sample was originally employed by the church to run the food bank, but since being made redundant he has been running it as a volunteer.
'Rollercoaster' project
The food bank, which supports about 50-60 families and individuals each week, will continue to run until January.
Sample described his time at the food bank as a "rollercoaster", and said he had some "stressful times" as well as some times when he encountered heart-warming moments.
He said: "We've encountered people struggling with grief and their world falling in around about them, and they've come to us for help.
"We've done what we do and a couple of years later, they've been back and brought us stuff, so it's been very good that way."
Sample thanked all the "unbelievable" volunteers who have supported the food bank over the years.
He said he would be "happy" if someone came forward to take on the food bank, but they would need to find new funding streams to keep operating the project.

title: Sebastián Lelio, director of A Fantastic Woman and Gloria, dies aged 52
content_c:
Chilean film-maker Sebastián Lelio has died at the age of 52.
He was best known for the Oscar-winning trans drama A Fantastic Woman and his English-language films included Gloria Bell and The Wonder.
His partner Amalia Kassai announced his death on Instagram without specifying the cause of death but telling followers, in Spanish, that it was a painful time for his family. Chilean media reports that he died at his home in Las Condes, Santiago.
Lelio was born in Argentina but moved to Chile at the age of two. He studied journalism for one year before graduating from film school and then released 9/11 documentary Cero in 2003. His first narrative film The Sacred Family premiered at the San Sebastián film festival in 2005.
His follow-up, 2009’s Christmas, premiered at Cannes but it was 2013’s Gloria that provided him with a major international breakthrough. The drama, about a woman in her late 50s who starts dating again, premiered at Berlin and won its lead star Paulina García an acting award at the festival.
Lelio followed it up with A Fantastic Woman, a drama about the life of a trans woman, another breakout that became the first Chilean film to win the Oscar for best international feature. In a five-star review, the Guardian’s Peter Bradshaw called it “a sublime study in the exalted ordeal of grief”.
“When we released it in 2017, a gender identity bill had been dormant in congress for seven years,” he said in a Guardian interview in 2018. “Somehow, the film’s release, and the year in which it became globally known, helped to reactivate the discussion in Chile.”
He made his English language debut with London-set drama Disobedience which told a queer love story between women played by Rachel Weisz and Rachel McAdams. It was nominated for five British independent film awards.
Lelio then remade Gloria as Gloria Bell, then set in America and starring Julianne Moore in the lead role. He followed it with a critically acclaimed adaptation of Emma Donoghue’s novel The Wonder starring Florence Pugh.
“I love working with actors, and need to know they trust me and can explore, get lost, be foolish or brave, and I’ll take care of them,” he said to the Guardian. “I love working on set – it is where the sparkle is.”
His final film was 2025’s The Wave, a musical protest drama that premiered at Cannes.
“Making a film is like a gift you leave somewhere – you then hide and see what happens,” he said.

title: ‘Profound anger’ among black voters over Kemi Badenoch’s slavery remarks
content_c:
The Conservative leader, Kemi Badenoch, has caused “profound anger, hurt and disbelief” among many black voters with her comments about transatlantic slavery, according to the chair of Operation Black Vote (OBV), who urged the prime minister, Andy Burnham, to apologise for Britain’s involvement without delay.
David Weaver, a former government adviser, said the Labour and Tory leaders risked alienating black voters with their handling of the issue of a state apology for slavery, while saying Badenoch’s remarks showed a “troubling absence of moral leadership”.
In a week in which the UK political agenda was dominated by postcolonial legacies, Badenoch said Burnham should not apologise for Britain’s historical role in slavery “because it is a lever to wedge open the door to ask for cash”, while criticising Commonwealth leaders on X.
Burnham, while saying he was open to making a formal apology on behalf of the British state, has ruled out reparations. Weaver said he welcomed the prime minister’s apparent willingness to apologise, but said the government’s “almost reflexive insistence” that any apology must come with assurances “reparations are off the table” was concerning.
Weaver said only the prime minister had the power to address the hurt felt by descendant communities and show Britain had the “moral courage to apologise without qualification”.
But he said Badenoch’s comments highlighted wider concerns about the UK’s political climate, adding: “At Operation Black Vote, we are hearing profound anger, hurt and disbelief.”
He added: “For us, this is not an abstract historical debate. It concerns our families, our heritage and our humanity. Political leaders should not underestimate the depth of feeling within black communities or their democratic power.”
Weaver said that in seeking an apology, Commonwealth nations wanted recognition of continuing colonial legacies that hampered development, and that Badenoch’s comments were “profoundly insulting”.
This week marked the second anniversary of Badenoch becoming the first black woman to lead a major British political party. OBV, a national, non-partisan civil rights group founded in 1996, welcomed her historic achievement in becoming Tory leader in 2024.
Meanwhile, although black voters were more likely than any other voters to have backed Labour in the 2024 general election, Weaver said OBV had found they felt “despondent” with the party and “taken for granted”, in particular over its handling of the consequences of the Windrush scandal.
Weaver added: “All parties should understand that to not apologise for slavery, the worst crime against humanity, is an insult. An apology should not have to be begged for. It should be an expression of genuine remorse and moral responsibility, not a carefully managed political statement designed to demonstrate toughness or avoid obligation.
“Reparative justice is not just about money. Ending an injustice does not erase responsibility for perpetrating it. We must ask why acknowledging this particular historical injustice remains so difficult and whether deeper racial attitudes continue to shape the debate.”
Badenoch, who has advocated a “colour-blind” approach to race, has long argued that people from ethnic minorities should be free to express differing views on race without being accused of betraying their communities.
But while attempting to frame herself as a unifier, Badenoch has given roles to the hard-right politician Rupert Lowe, Katie Lam – the MP who said a “large number” of legal migrants “need to go home” – and the former neo-Nazi Joshua Bonehill-Paine, while outlining plans to scrap the public sector equality duty and leave the European court of human rights.
Weaver said: “She’s the leader of the Conservative party. That’s a big deal. She’s got a high popularity rating and can be very effective. But many black voters tell us there’s a lot of mistrust for her lack of empathy – and because she will sometimes say things her white counterparts could not say and get away with it. So she becomes the front for unacceptable views on race.
“The current state of public discourse – and the silence when it comes to challenging it – contributes to a sense among black communities that they are being treated with contempt across the political spectrum.
“This is not just about Badenoch. Just because you’re black doesn’t mean you have to hold a particular point of view. But your heritage, whether you are white or black, does not place your views beyond challenge. An apology for slavery is about humanity and decency and seeing people’s worth. Andy Burnham must do the right thing – and soon.”
Downing Street and the Conservative party were approached for comment. Commonwealth leaders have said the UK has agreed to “structured dialogue” in the next year.

title: Pope Leo arrives in Uruguay at start of South America tour
content_c:
Pope Leo arrives in Uruguay at start of South America tour
November 6, 2026
Pope Leo XIV arrived in Uruguay on Friday at the start of a grueling 12-day tour through three South American countries, just weeks after his lung cancer surgery.
The 71-year-old pontiff told reporters he was very happy to be in Uruguay, having flown a nearly 14-hour flight from Rome to get to Montevideo.
"I confess that from the first day, I had no doubt and was convinced that this trip had to go forward," he told reporters aboard the papal plane.
Leo hit the ground running on arrival, drawing huge crowds in Montevideo as he pulled into town in his open-sided popemobile.
The Vatican estimated 30,000 people had turned out to watch him go by and attend his first event in a country that is largely secular and where membership in the Church is declining.
"In an age when differences can easily become a source of conflict, persevering in respect for the law, negotiation and the patient search for agreements is a service that Uruguay can continue to offer its neighbors," Leo told crowds in Montevideo's main square.
Uruguayan President Yamandu Orsi, leader of the center-left alliance, was present there too.
Leo is then planning to visit the Casavalle neighborhood, which is notorious for its high rates of poverty and violence.
With starting in Uruguay, Leo marks the first papal visit to the country in nearly four decades, with Pope John Paul II having last visited in 1988.
What to know about Pope Leo's taxing itinerary
The pontiff will spend three days in Uruguay before heading on to Argentina on Sunday.
He then travels to Peru, where he spent half his priestly life, before he was elected pontiff last year. He became a naturalized Peruvian citizen in 2015.
Latin America is home to around 40% of the world's 1.4 billion Catholics, for whom the pope is their spiritual leader. However, fewer and fewer people on the continent identify as Catholic.
Enthusiasm around Leo's visit a surprise in Uruguay
Uruguay, the most secular Latin American country, was the first country in the world to legalize recreational marijuana use and has since legalized abortion, same-sex marriage and assisted dying, all against opposition from the Catholic Church.
However, the enthusiasm around Leo's visit has come as a bit of a surprise, with tickets for his prayer vigil at Montevideo's Centenario Stadium selling out in just two days.
What will Pope Leo do in Argentina?
On Sunday, Leo will cross over to neighboring Argentina, the home of his papal predecessor Francis, who, however, disappointed his native compatriots by never returning home as pope.
At the beginning of Francis's papacy, some 71% of Argentinians identified as Catholic, according to the Pew Research Center. By 2024, this had fallen to 58%.
Leo is set to meet with Argentinian President Javier Milei, who has come under criticism from the Catholic Church for his sweeping cuts that have hampered programs for the poor and needy.
He is also planning to meet with business leaders, trade unions, workers and social representatives.
Pope Leo to return to Peru for last leg of trip
The final leg of the trip, on Wednesday, will see Leo return to Peru, where he lived and preached for two decades.
There is excitement about his visit to Peru, with the pope planning to celebrate Mass in his old diocese of Chiclayo as well as in the mountain village of Santa Cruz de Succhabamba.
The pope will also celebrate Mass in the former Incan capital city of Cusco before honoring Peru's indigenous population by traveling to Pucallpa in the Peruvian Amazon.
The excitement can be seen in the street vendors selling T-shirts and rosaries with his likeness, while bakeries have been selling Leo bread.
Peru has also seen a weakening of the faithful in recent years, with the Catholic population falling from 76% in 2013-2014 to around 67% now.

Pope Leo arrives in Uruguay at start of South America tour
November 6, 2026
Pope Leo XIV arrived in Uruguay on Friday at the start of a grueling 12-day tour through three South American countries, just weeks after his lung cancer surgery.
The 71-year-old pontiff told reporters he was very happy to be in Uruguay, having flown a nearly 14-hour flight from Rome to get to Montevideo.
"I confess that from the first day, I had no doubt and was convinced that this trip had to go forward," he told reporters aboard the papal plane.
Leo hit the ground running on arrival, drawing huge crowds in Montevideo as he pulled into town in his open-sided popemobile.
The Vatican estimated 30,000 people had turned out to watch him go by and attend his first event in a country that is largely secular and where membership in the Church is declining.
"In an age when differences can easily become a source of conflict, persevering in respect for the law, negotiation and the patient search for agreements is a service that Uruguay can continue to offer its neighbors," Leo told crowds in Montevideo's main square.
Uruguayan President Yamandu Orsi, leader of the center-left alliance, was present there too.
Leo is then planning to visit the Casavalle neighborhood, which is notorious for its high rates of poverty and violence.
With starting in Uruguay, Leo marks the first papal visit to the country in nearly four decades, with Pope John Paul II having last visited in 1988.

title: Gerät Tschechiens Wasserwirtschaft in Gefahr?
content_c:
Regen- und Schneemangel Gerät Tschechiens Wasserhaushalt in Gefahr?
Seit zwei Jahren gibt es in Tschechien zu wenig Schnee und Regen - der wasserreichste Stausee ist mittlerweile halb leer. Sollte auch dieser Winter die Pegelstände nicht anheben, wäre die Versorgung im ganzen Land gefährdet.
Pavel Patera steigt hinab - erst die Stufen des neuen Bootsanlegers, dann muss er klettern, um in sein Kontrollboot zu gelangen. Er ist der Leiter des Orlik-Stauwerks, des wasserreichsten Stausees in Tschechien. Patera erzählt, dass man erst vor zwei Jahren die Treppe neu gebaut habe. Keiner habe damals vermutet, dass der Pegel einmal so tief fallen würde. Bei dem Anblick des Sees blute ihm das Herz.
Ganze 15 Meter ist der Pegel des Stausees schon gefallen - und hat damit die Hälfte seines Wassers verloren. Hier, kurz hinter der Staumauer, wirkt der Wasserverlust auf den ersten Blick minimal, doch an den Rändern zeichnet sich der alte Wasserstand ab.
An den Rändern des Stausees wird deutlich, welche Auswirkungen die Trockenheit in Tschechien hier hat.
Zu wenig Regen, zu wenig Schnee
So niedrig war der Pegel zuletzt vor 50 Jahren. Vor allem die Seitenarme des Stausees laufen trocken. An der Podolsky Most, rund 25 Kilometer Luftlinie von der Staumauer entfernt, tauchen die Reste eines alten Gasthofes wieder auf.
Daneben kommen die Pfeiler der alten Seilbrücke aus dem 19. Jahrhundert wieder zum Vorschein. Der Pegel an der neuen Brücke zeigt schon seit Wochen keinen Wasserstand mehr an. Selbst in der Nähe der Staumauer wurden Gebäuderuinen im See mit kleinen selbstgemachten Bojen markiert - wie etwa der alte Kirchturm, der noch unter Wasser liegt.
Patera hofft, dass das auch so bleibt, denn seit zwei Jahren gab es in Tschechien zu wenig Schnee und Regen. Der vergangene Sommer war nach Angaben von Hydrologen der trockenste seit 80 Jahren.
Stauwerkschef Patera sagt, dass Prag in die Wasserversorgung des Landes investieren müsse.
Sorge um die Moldau
Doch davon merkt man in der Landeshauptstadt Prag nichts; zumindest noch nicht. Denn der Orlik-Stausee gehört zur sogenannten Moldau-Kaskade. Das sind neun Staubecken vom Böhmerwald bis kurz vor Prag.
Sie dienen dem Hochwasserschutz, doch bei Dürre geben sie Wasser ab und halten den Pegel der Moldau auf einem Mindestmaß. Noch können andere Teile der Kaskade genügend Wasser bereitstellen, so dass die Pegel in Prag stabil bleiben.
Das Stausystem diene aber nicht nur der Hauptstadt, es versorge viele Regionen Tschechiens, erklärt Petr Kubala, Direktor der Flussgebietsverwaltung Moldau. Mit dem Wasser der Seen würde das gesamte Ökosystem rings um den Fluss am Leben gehalten. Es sorge dafür, dass die Wasserentnahme, beispielsweise für die Landwirtschaft, funktioniere, dass eingeleitete Abwässer verdünnt würden, und dass der Grundwasserspiegel in der folgenden Elbe-Region stabil bleibe.
Auch Kubala blickt sorgenvoll auf den Fluss. Noch ein weiterer Dürrewinter würde nicht nur die Moldau-Kaskade sondern die gesamte Wasserwirtschaft in Tschechien in Gefahr bringen.
20 neue Stauseen oder Rekultivierung?
Die Regierung Babis verspricht deshalb 20 neue Stauwerke - sie sollen noch mehr Wasser für Dürren bereithalten. Doch deren Finanzierung ist völlig unklar. Im tschechischen Haushalt klafft ein Milliardenloch, und ob die EU dafür Fördermittel bereitstellt, ist offen. Außerdem dauert der Bau von Staumauern Jahre; am Orlik-See wurde sieben Jahre gearbeitet.
Auch deshalb schlägt Direktor Petr Kubala, der auch die Regierung berät, kurzfristigere Maßnahmen vor. So müsse die Landwirtschaft mehr Versickerungsflächen schaffen, alte Bach- und Flussläufe sollten rekultiviert werden. Das Ziel müsse sein, das Wasser besser zu speichern statt es abzuleiten.
Das sieht auch Pavel Patera am Orlik-Stausee so. Auch er ist überzeugt, dass Tschechien in seine Wasserversorgung investieren muss. Vielleicht könne er irgendwann die neuen 20 Stausee-Chefs begrüßen, sagt er. Doch bis dahin sei es ein weiter Weg.
Jetzt hofft Patera erstmal auf Regen: Viel Regen - denn ein richtig nasser Herbst und Winter würden seinen See wieder auffüllen.
Diese und weitere Reportagen sehen Sie im Europamagazin - am Sonntag um 12:45 Uhr im Ersten.

title: Wie Berlins arabische Queers ihre Community aufbauen
content_c:
Wie Berlins arabische Queers ihre Community aufbauen
6. November 2026
"Adira" ist ein arabischer Slangbegriff aus der queeren Kultur des östlichen Mittelmeerraums. Er bezeichnet Menschen mit starker Präsenz, die als kraftvoll und erfolgreich gelten.
ADIRA ist auch der Name eines Berliner Kollektivs, das Veranstaltungen und Clubnächte organisiert, die die Vielfalt queerer arabischer* Kultur feiern. Das Sternchen hinter "arabisch" soll verdeutlichen, dass unter dem Begriff auch nichtarabische ethnische Minderheiten sowie Menschen mit unterschiedlichen Identitäten und Wurzeln in Südwestasien und Nordafrika mitgedacht werden.
Eine der Veranstaltungen des Kollektivs ist das "ADIRA Drag Festival", das Ende Oktober zum dritten Mal in Berlin stattfand. Unter dem Motto "Who's Your Diva?!" kamen Drag-Performende zusammen, die queeren Ikonen aus dem östlichen Mittelmeerraum Tribut zollten: von der ägyptischen Musiklegende Umm Kulthum über den türkischen Star Bülent Ersoy bis hin zur libanesischen Popikone Haifa Wehbe.
Hassandra hat ADIRA und das ADIRA Drag Festival mitbegründet und stand ebenfalls auf der Bühne - in der Rolle der libanesischen Popsängerin Elissa.
Diven als Vorbilder und Projektionsflächen
"Es ist mir sehr wichtig, meine libanesisch-arabische Identität und Kultur in meine Arbeit einzubringen, weil ich sie für eine sehr schöne Kultur halte. Und sie hat viele glamouröse und faszinierende Diven", sagt Hassandra.
Eine von ihnen ist die libanesische Popsängerin Elissa. Deren "gesamte Diskografie ist sehr romantisch, roh und sanft, fast mit Adele-Vibes", sagte Hassandra vor der Show im Gespräch mit DW. "Ihre Persönlichkeit gilt jedoch als das genaue Gegenteil. Sie ist sehr temperamentvoll, sehr direkt und ungefiltert. Als Mensch ist sie überhaupt nicht sanft."
Die Sängerin ist zudem dafür bekannt, sich zu politischen Themen im Libanon zu äußern. Sie hat sich öffentlich für LGBTQ+-Gemeinschaften im Nahen Osten ausgesprochen, zugleich aber mit ihren deutlichen Positionen zu anderen politischen Themen immer wieder Kontroversen in der arabischen Welt ausgelöst.
Beim Auftritt in Berlin greift Hassandra diese Komplexität auf und setzt sich mit Elissas teils umstrittenen politischen Ansichten auseinander. Das ist ganz im Sinne der Botschaft des Festivals: "Als queere Menschen neigen wir dazu, Pop-Diven zu idealisieren. Aber diese Pop-Diven sind in ihrem Wesen sehr unperfekt", sagt Hassandra. Die Show biete die Gelegenheit, das Vermächtnis dieser Diven noch einmal aus einer kritischeren Perspektive zu betrachten. Und im Grunde gelte das auch generell: "Man sollte im Leben niemandem blind folgen. Niemand sollte einem Politiker, einer politischen Partei, einer Pop-Diva oder einem Aktivisten blind folgen", so Hassandra.
Gemeinschaft durch Drag
Hassandra wurde 1994 in Beirut geboren und studierte Theater und Schauspiel an der Libanesischen Universität. 2017 zog Hassandra nach Berlin. "Es war eine sehr impulsive Entscheidung im Alter von 22 Jahren. Die wirtschaftliche Lage im Libanon war schlecht und es gab keine Aussichten." In Berlin wurde Hassandra nach und nach Teil der unabhängigen Kunstszene und des queeren Nachtlebens der Stadt. Drag entwickelte sich für Hassandra zu einer weiteren Form des Selbstausdrucks.
Mit Performances, die theatralische Intensität, politischen Humor, groteske Ästhetik und Momente der Zärtlichkeit verbinden, stellt Hassandra konventionelle Vorstellungen von Geschlecht und Identität infrage. Hassandra erkundet Themen wie Heimat, Nostalgie, Entwurzelung und queere arabische Kultur. 2023 gründete Hassandra ADIRA, zusammen mit dem syrisch-deutschen DJ und Kulturproduzenten Zuher Jazmati, der auch unter dem Namen xanax_attax bekannt ist.
Mit Podiumsdiskussionen, Performances und Musikveranstaltungen fördert ADIRA gesellschaftliche Teilhabe und den Aufbau von Gemeinschaft. Angesichts zunehmender Islamfeindlichkeit und Homophobie sowie des Erstarkens der extremen Rechten bieten Orte wie ADIRA arabischen queeren Gemeinschaften ein Gefühl von Zugehörigkeit und Unterstützung. Dieses Gemeinschaftsgefühl hat nach dem tödlichen islamistischen Terroranschlag während der Christopher-Street-Day-Parade in Berlin im Juli noch mehr an Bedeutung gewonnen.
Nach dem Anschlag fühlte sich Hassandra zwischen verschiedenen Identitäten gefangen. Als queere arabische Person gerate man in eine Situation, in der man plötzlich viel Rassismus erfahre. "Deshalb ist es wichtig, dass wir als queere arabische Menschen sagen, dass wir traurig sind über das, was passiert ist. Aber wir lehnen auch den Rassismus ab, der daraus entsteht." Hassandra hat den Eindruck, dass die arabische Gemeinschaft in vielerlei Hinsicht als Sündenbock herhalten müsse. Doch statt zuzulassen, dass der Anschlag weiteren Hass und Rassismus schürt, will Hassandra dazu beitragen, Deutschland zu einem "sichereren Ort für alle zu machen", denn: "Es gibt Platz für alle. Es ist ein riesiges Land."
Das Interview mit Hassandra führte Gönna Ketels. Adaption aus dem Englischen: Petra Lambeck
description: Hassandra gehört zu den bekanntesten Stimmen der queeren arabischen Kunstszene in Berlin. Mit dem 2023 gegründeten ADIRA Drag Festival schafft Hassandra gemeinsam mit anderen, Räume für Austausch und Gemeinschaft.

"Es ist mir sehr wichtig, meine libanesisch-arabische Identität und Kultur in meine Arbeit einzubringen, weil ich sie für eine sehr schöne Kultur halte. Und sie hat viele glamouröse und faszinierende Diven", sagt Hassandra.
Eine von ihnen ist die libanesische Popsängerin Elissa. Deren "gesamte Diskografie ist sehr romantisch, roh und sanft, fast mit Adele-Vibes", sagte Hassandra vor der Show im Gespräch mit DW. "Ihre Persönlichkeit gilt jedoch als das genaue Gegenteil. Sie ist sehr temperamentvoll, sehr direkt und ungefiltert. Als Mensch ist sie überhaupt nicht sanft."
Die Sängerin ist zudem dafür bekannt, sich zu politischen Themen im Libanon zu äußern. Sie hat sich öffentlich für LGBTQ+-Gemeinschaften im Nahen Osten ausgesprochen, zugleich aber mit ihren deutlichen Positionen zu anderen politischen Themen immer wieder Kontroversen in der arabischen Welt ausgelöst.
Beim Auftritt in Berlin greift Hassandra diese Komplexität auf und setzt sich mit Elissas teils umstrittenen politischen Ansichten auseinander. Das ist ganz im Sinne der Botschaft des Festivals: "Als queere Menschen neigen wir dazu, Pop-Diven zu idealisieren. Aber diese Pop-Diven sind in ihrem Wesen sehr unperfekt", sagt Hassandra. Die Show biete die Gelegenheit, das Vermächtnis dieser Diven noch einmal aus einer kritischeren Perspektive zu betrachten. Und im Grunde gelte das auch generell: "Man sollte im Leben niemandem blind folgen. Niemand sollte einem Politiker, einer politischen Partei, einer Pop-Diva oder einem Aktivisten blind folgen", so Hassandra.
Gemeinschaft durch Drag
Hassandra wurde 1994 in Beirut geboren und studierte Theater und Schauspiel an der Libanesischen Universität. 2017 zog Hassandra nach Berlin. "Es war eine sehr impulsive Entscheidung im Alter von 22 Jahren. Die wirtschaftliche Lage im Libanon war schlecht und es gab keine Aussichten." In Berlin wurde Hassandra nach und nach Teil der unabhängigen Kunstszene und des queeren Nachtlebens der Stadt. Drag entwickelte sich für Hassandra zu einer weiteren Form des Selbstausdrucks.
Mit Performances, die theatralische Intensität, politischen Humor, groteske Ästhetik und Momente der Zärtlichkeit verbinden, stellt Hassandra konventionelle Vorstellungen von Geschlecht und Identität infrage. Hassandra erkundet Themen wie Heimat, Nostalgie, Entwurzelung und queere arabische Kultur. 2023 gründete Hassandra ADIRA, zusammen mit dem syrisch-deutschen DJ und Kulturproduzenten Zuher Jazmati, der auch unter dem Namen xanax_attax bekannt ist.
Mit Podiumsdiskussionen, Performances und Musikveranstaltungen fördert ADIRA gesellschaftliche Teilhabe und den Aufbau von Gemeinschaft. Angesichts zunehmender Islamfeindlichkeit und Homophobie sowie des Erstarkens der extremen Rechten bieten Orte wie ADIRA arabischen queeren Gemeinschaften ein Gefühl von Zugehörigkeit und Unterstützung. Dieses Gemeinschaftsgefühl hat nach dem tödlichen islamistischen Terroranschlag während der Christopher-Street-Day-Parade in Berlin im Juli noch mehr an Bedeutung gewonnen.
Nach dem Anschlag fühlte sich Hassandra zwischen verschiedenen Identitäten gefangen. Als queere arabische Person gerate man in eine Situation, in der man plötzlich viel Rassismus erfahre. "Deshalb ist es wichtig, dass wir als queere arabische Menschen sagen, dass wir traurig sind über das, was passiert ist. Aber wir lehnen auch den Rassismus ab, der daraus entsteht." Hassandra hat den Eindruck, dass die arabische Gemeinschaft in vielerlei Hinsicht als Sündenbock herhalten müsse. Doch statt zuzulassen, dass der Anschlag weiteren Hass und Rassismus schürt, will Hassandra dazu beitragen, Deutschland zu einem "sichereren Ort für alle zu machen", denn: "Es gibt Platz für alle. Es ist ein riesiges Land."
Das Interview mit Hassandra führte Gönna Ketels. Adaption aus dem Englischen: Petra Lambeck

title: Великий обласний центр накрив блекаут: що відбувається у місті
content_c:
Великий обласний центр накрив блекаут: що відбувається у місті
Чернігів повністю знеструмлено: у місті не ходить електротранспорт.
Зранку 7 листопада Чернігів повністю залишився без електропостачання. В обласному центрі не працює електротранспорт.
Що відомо про відключення світла у Чернігові — читайте на ТСН.ua.
Зранку у пресслужбі Чернігівської міської ради повідомили про складну ситуацією з енергетикою.
«Наразі місто Чернігів повністю знеструмлене», — йдеться у повідомленні.
Зазначається, що у зв’язку з відсутністю світла в місті тимчасово зупинили рух електричного громадського транспорту.
Ситуація в енергетиці — останні новини
Цієї ночі армія РФ знову пошкодила енергетику, зокрема на Київщині та Житомирщині. За даними столичної влади, через «прильоти» склалася складна ситуація з енергозабезпеченням Києва, а також у роботі систем тепло- та водопостачання.
Зауважимо, «Укренерго» запровадило графіки погодинних відключень світла на 7 листопада. За попередніми даними, протягом доби відключатимуть від 2 до 4 черг споживачів одночасно у різних областях України.

title: Собор Архангела Михаила: традиции
content_c:
В праздник верующие посещали храмы.
8 ноября христиане восточного обряда отмечают Собор Архистратига Михаила и других Небесных Сил бесплотных. Праздник посвящен архангелу Михаилу, который считается главой небесных сил — архистратигом. Народное название праздника — Михайлов день.
Что нужно делать в Михайлов день
Традиционно в Собор Архангела Михаила верующие посещали богослужения в церквях. В молитвах они обращались к архангелу Михаилу и просили защиты от злых сил. Если нет возможности пойти в храм на праздник, можно прочитать молитву дома.
Раньше считалось, что в этот день каждый получает по заслугам, а грешников ждет наказание.
В древности в этот праздник существовала традиция устраивать гуляния и приглашать гостей. Это делали потому, что после Михайлового день начинался Рождественский пост, когда действовали ограничения в еде. В этот день на стол обязательно подавали мясное блюдо.
Молитва к Архистратигу Михаилу
О, Великий Архистратиг Божий, Михаил, победитель демонов. Победи и сокруши всех моих демонов, видимых и невидимых. Умоли Господа Вседержителя, да спасет и сохранит меня Господь от всех скорбей и болезней, от смертоносной язвы и от напрасной смерти, о, Великий Архангел Михаил, ныне и во все времена и во веки веков. Аминь.

title: Трамп обіцяє "велику, чудову угоду", яка має вийти за межі України
content_c:
Трамп обіцяє "велику, чудову угоду", яка має вийти за межі України
  - Author, Відділ новин
  - Role, ВВС News Україна
- Published
- Час прочитання: 3 хв
Президент США Дональд Трамп заявив, що найближчим часом може бути укладена велика угода щодо України. За його словами, вона стосуватиметься не лише завершення війни, а "може охопити всю Європу".
5 листопада, спілкуючись з журналістами в Білому домі, Трамп заявив, що розраховує на масштабні домовленості, які виходитимуть далеко за межі завершення російсько-української війни.
"Буде угода, буде велика угода, і вона охопить не лише Україну".
"І я навіть можу сказати, що вона, можливо, стосуватиметься всієї Європи. Це буде велика, чудова угода, і всі будуть у захваті", — додав американський президент.
Що саме передбачатиме ця угода, Трамп не пояснив. Він також не уточнив, які питання можуть стати предметом домовленостей.
Американський президент повідомив, що зустрічався у Вашингтоні зі спеціальним представником російського лідера Володимира Путіна Кирилом Дмитрієвим. Водночас, за його словами, з українською делегацією він не зустрічався.
Трамп не розповів, чи обговорював з Дмитрієвим умови припинення війни та можливі параметри майбутньої угоди.
Кирило Дмитрієв прибув до США, щоб зустрітися з першою леді Меланією Трамп. У четвер вона розповіла про свою участь у переговорах щодо перемир'я в Олешках на Херсонщині.
У зустрічі також брали участь український омбудсмен Дмитро Лубінець, голова фракції "Слуга народу" Давид Арахамія та російська уповноважена з прав людини Яна Лантратова.
Кушнер розкрив, про що США хочуть домовитися з Україною та Росією в Абу-Дабі
На тлі заяв Трампа його спеціальний посланник Джаред Кушнер підтвердив, що наступного тижня в Абу-Дабі відбудуться тристоронні мирні переговори за участю України, США та Росії.
За його словами, це будуть перші переговори такого формату з лютого.
"Ми працювали з обома сторонами, щоб підготувати серйозні пропозиції та зробити ці переговори максимально змістовними й результативними", - написав Кушнер у соцмережі X.
Він наголосив, що Трамп вважає досягнення миру одним зі своїх головних пріоритетів. Американська сторона, за його словами, працює над всеосяжною угодою, яка має забезпечити тривалий мир.
Кушнер також розповів, що американська делегація провела в Брюсселі переговори з Україною, НАТО та європейськими партнерами.
Головними темами стали гарантії безпеки для України та майбутня система безпеки в Європі.
"Ми активно працюємо з усіма сторонами, щоб знайти практичні рішення, які допоможуть завершити цю війну та закласти основу для тривалого миру", - заявив він.
Чого Україна хоче від переговорів в Абу-Дабі
Переговори в Абу-Дабі заплановані на 10-11 листопада.
Росію на переговорах представлятиме Володимир Мединський.
Ще 28 жовтня помічник Путіна Юрій Ушаков повідомляв, що консультації України, США та Росії можуть відбутися після 4 листопада. Тоді він пояснював, що дата залежатиме від ситуації на фронті та загальної обстановки.
Україна хотіла провести зустріч до 10 листопада - перед можливими контактами США, Китаю та Росії на саміті АТЕС у Шеньчжені.
Президент України Володимир Зеленський раніше повідомив, що Київ хоче обговорити в Абу-Дабі кілька важливих питань.
Серед них - припинення ударів по енергетичній та критичній інфраструктурі, розблокування Чорного моря та активізація обміну полоненими.
Україна також наполягає на зустрічі Зеленського та Путіна за посередництва США.
Київ хоче, щоб у переговорному процесі брали участь і європейські партнери.
Зеленський заявляв, що Україна не відмовлятиметься від тристоронньої зустрічі, якщо США наполягатимуть на такому форматі. Водночас він наголошував, що участь Європи важлива для майбутньої безпеки України.
Найскладнішим питанням залишаються території.
Зеленський багато разів підкреслював, що Україна не погоджується на територіальні поступки. За його словами, обговорювати такі питання можна лише на рівні лідерів держав.
Кремль розраховує затягнути війну
Дипломатичні контакти відбуваються на тлі серйозних розбіжностей між Москвою та Вашингтоном.
На початку листопада Bloomberg повідомив, що в Кремлі все менше вірять у те, що Трамп зможе змусити Україну погодитися на російські умови.
За даними агентства, Москва тепер розраховує затягнути війну, посилити удари по Україні та тиск на її європейських союзників.
Росія продовжує вимагати передачі під свій контроль неокупованих територій Донбасу та політичних змін в Україні.

Він наголосив, що Трамп вважає досягнення миру одним зі своїх головних пріоритетів. Американська сторона, за його словами, працює над всеосяжною угодою, яка має забезпечити тривалий мир.
Кушнер також розповів, що американська делегація провела в Брюсселі переговори з Україною, НАТО та європейськими партнерами.
Головними темами стали гарантії безпеки для України та майбутня система безпеки в Європі.
"Ми активно працюємо з усіма сторонами, щоб знайти практичні рішення, які допоможуть завершити цю війну та закласти основу для тривалого миру", - заявив він.
Чого Україна хоче від переговорів в Абу-Дабі
Переговори в Абу-Дабі заплановані на 10-11 листопада.
Росію на переговорах представлятиме Володимир Мединський.
Ще 28 жовтня помічник Путіна Юрій Ушаков повідомляв, що консультації України, США та Росії можуть відбутися після 4 листопада. Тоді він пояснював, що дата залежатиме від ситуації на фронті та загальної обстановки.
Україна хотіла провести зустріч до 10 листопада - перед можливими контактами США, Китаю та Росії на саміті АТЕС у Шеньчжені.
Президент України Володимир Зеленський раніше повідомив, що Київ хоче обговорити в Абу-Дабі кілька важливих питань.
Серед них - припинення ударів по енергетичній та критичній інфраструктурі, розблокування Чорного моря та активізація обміну полоненими.
Україна також наполягає на зустрічі Зеленського та Путіна за посередництва США.
Київ хоче, щоб у переговорному процесі брали участь і європейські партнери.
Зеленський заявляв, що Україна не відмовлятиметься від тристоронньої зустрічі, якщо США наполягатимуть на такому форматі. Водночас він наголошував, що участь Європи важлива для майбутньої безпеки України.
Найскладнішим питанням залишаються території.
Зеленський багато разів підкреслював, що Україна не погоджується на територіальні поступки. За його словами, обговорювати такі питання можна лише на рівні лідерів держав.
Кремль розраховує затягнути війну
Дипломатичні контакти відбуваються на тлі серйозних розбіжностей між Москвою та Вашингтоном.
На початку листопада Bloomberg повідомив, що в Кремлі все менше вірять у те, що Трамп зможе змусити Україну погодитися на російські умови.
За даними агентства, Москва тепер розраховує затягнути війну, посилити удари по Україні та тиск на її європейських союзників.
Росія продовжує вимагати передачі під свій контроль неокупованих територій Донбасу та політичних змін в Україні.

title: Троє людей, серед них дитина постраждали унаслідок російської атаки в Києві, пошкоджено багатоповерхівку
content_c:
Державна служба України з надзвичайних ситуацій повідомляє про трьох постраждалих у Києві внаслідок атаки РФ в ніч на суботу.
"У Солом'янському районі виникли пожежі та зафіксовано руйнування і пошкодження житлових будинків, дитячого садка й нежитлової будівлі. За однією з адрес частково зруйновано фасад першого поверху п'ятиповерхового житлового будинку. Загоряння не було, загиблих і постраждалих немає", – повідомляється в телеграм-каналі ДСНС.
Ще за трьома адресами вибуховою хвилею вибило вікна в п'ятиповерхових будинках, одна людина отримала травми.
Також зафіксовано руйнування двоповерхової будівлі на території дитячого садка. На іншій локації горіли припаркована вантажівка та нежитлова будівля. Пожежу ліквідовано.
За ще двома адресами постраждали двоє людей, серед них дитина. Загалом унаслідок атаки травмовано троє людей.

title: Paraguay's President Santiago Peña impeached and arrested
content_c:
Paraguay's President Santiago Peña impeached and arrested
- Published
Paraguay's President Santiago Peña has been impeached and placed under house arrest after the collapse of a digital bank with links to his private business interests.
Peña was arrested on Friday minutes after lawmakers, including from his own party, unanimously voted to remove him from office due to a widening crisis triggered by the collapse of Ueno Bank earlier this week.
He had offered to step down on Thursday. Rather than accept his resignation, senators impeached Peña and charged him with misconduct, meaning he has been stripped of the immunity usually granted to ex-presidents.
Peña, who until last year held shares in the company that owned the bank, has denied any wrongdoing.
The demise of the digital bank has left more than half of Paraguay's population without access to their savings after it was seized by Paraguay's central bank.
An estimated three million depositors remain unable to access their savings and pensions prompting widespread protests particularly in the capital, Asunción.
The impeachment charges that led to Peña's removal alleged he had conflicts of interest, manipulated regulatory oversight, diverted pension funds, and participated in an institutional cover-up involving the central bank.
Peña is due to be questioned on Saturday over allegations of breach of trust, influence peddling, and misappropriation of funds, prosecutor Silvia Margarita Gonzalez Vester said.
Peña's impeachment passed with 44 out of 45 senators voting in favour of it. One lawmaker was absent.
Afterwards, senate president Basilio Núñez said Peña was found guilty of "dereliction of duty".
Paraguay's Vice-President Pedro Alliana was then sworn in as interim President.
"Compatriots who are now going through a difficult time as a result of the financial collapse will be fully compensated," said Alliana, who will serve as President until 2028.
Senator Rafael Filizzola said: "We are facing the biggest corruption scandal in our democratic history – a tremendous blow to the state, to private citizens, and to the country's credibility and image."
Analysts say Peña is likely to now be prosecuted over the bank's collapse.
His defence lawyer Ricardo Preda described the allegations as a "reckless accusation" that was "irresponsible and opportunistic".
In an address to the nation on Thursday, Peña said that he was sorry and that "it was never my intention to betray the trust you placed in me".

title: Algorithm allocates Highland 'significant increase' in asylum-seeking children
content_c:
Algorithm allocates Highland 'significant increase' in asylum-seeking children
- Published
Highland Council says a Home Office algorithm has allocated it with a "significant increase" in unaccompanied asylum-seeking children to look after.
The local authority said it had received national recognition for its work with the young people, many of them fleeing war or persecution.
But it said the rise in numbers would be challenging due to a lack of housing in its area, adding that the algorithm did not take into account the local situation.
The Home Office said councils had a statutory duty to support children arriving in the UK without a parent or guardian, and it was committed to working closely with authorities to help them meet their obligations.
Unaccompanied asylum-seeking children (UASC) are those under the age of 18 who arrive in the UK to apply for international protection on their own, without the support of an adult.
Many of them are fleeing their homeland because of political or religious persecution, war or famine.
There are 380 UASCs being looked after in Scotland, according to Scottish government figures for 31 July 2025, external.
Highland Council is currently responsible for 72.
The council said it was contacted by local authorities body Cosla in July about a revised Home Office rota allocation formula.
In a report, external, officials said this had presented it with "significant challenges" and five times its previous number of UASCs.
Previously, Highland Council took into its care system one child per cycle, but this has now gone up to five.
There can be a period of two weeks to a number of months between cycle, depending on how many children arrive in the UK.
'Not an adequate tool'
Highland Council officials added: "The Home Office algorithm by itself is not an adequate tool without some understanding of local conditions.
"For example, the fact that Highland has significant housing challenges, both in terms of housing availability and cost, coupled with a lack of available workforce, means Highland is not an attractive option for asylum support providers."
The local authority has previously said its area needs an extra 24,000 houses over the next 10 years. New homes are needed to address a long-standing shortage of affordable homes.
The officials also said the Home Office had not so far placed any adult asylum seekers in the Highlands.
"This lack of adult asylum seekers in Highland has had the effect of increasing the number of UASC in 2026," they said.
In June, the UK government scrapped plans to house up to 300 male asylum seekers at Cameron Barracks in Inverness.
'Shared fairly'
Eligible UASCs, like other young people in foster, kinship or residential care can remain under local authority care up to the age of 21.
Some care leavers are eligible for support up to their 26th birthday.
Highland Council receives core funding of £143 per child, per day for under 18s. For over 18s it is £270 per week.
The Home Office said it was a priority to ensure vulnerable children received the care and support they needed.
A spokesperson said: ''Local authorities have a statutory duty to support unaccompanied asylum-seeking children and care leavers, and we are committed to working closely with them to help them meet these obligations.
"Through the National Transfer Scheme, we work with local authorities across the UK to ensure responsibility for supporting unaccompanied children is shared fairly."

title: Winter support for residents facing cost pressures
content_c:
Winter support for residents facing cost pressures
- Published
Plans have been announced to help more people access affordable food, financial advice and help with heating costs this winter.
New community shops are due to open in Pendeford and Graiseley and a shop in Bilston is set to reopen. About 17,000 people have used Wolverhampton's network of community shops over the past six months, said City of Wolverhampton Council.
But council leader Stephen Simkins said many residents still faced difficult choices over household bills. "We know times are still tough for many residents," he added.
The council said more than 135,000 people have received support through its cost-of-living programmes, while more than £18.5m has been distributed to residents.
Simkins said: "Our ambition is simple, we want Wolverhampton to be a city where everyone has the opportunity to live a safe, secure and happy life.
"This winter, we will protect the most vulnerable and ensure nobody is left behind."
The new measures have been announced alongside the launch of a new three-year financial wellbeing strategy to support residents struggling with living costs.
About three tonnes of food are redistributed each month through weekly community markets, with plans to expand the scheme during the winter.
The authority is also extending its Community Chefs programme into schools.
More than 1,000 people have taken part in the initiative in the past six months, producing about 6,000 meals, said the council.
The Boost financial wellbeing service, launched in January to help residents reduce costs and manage household budgets, will also be expanded through the winter.
The council said winter warm packs have already been distributed through the city's family hubs, while adult social care teams are working with health services to help reduce seasonal pressures on the NHS.

title: Flávio Bolsonaro battles to remain relevant as he speaks at rightwing conference at Mar-a-Lago
content_c:
Flávio Bolsonaro, the far-right politician who lost Brazil’s presidential election last month, has insisted his defeat is not “the end for Brazil” as he battles to maintain political relevance after fleeing to the US.
Bolsonaro absconded early last week shortly after losing the 25 October election to the leftwing incumbent Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva by more than 4m votes.
On Thursday night Bolsonaro made his first major public appearance since arriving in the US, speaking at a rightwing gathering at Donald Trump’s Mar-a-Lago property where he claimed “great things” were still to come.
“I know this wasn’t the end for Brazil and I know it wasn’t the end for America,” Bolsonaro, 45, told a gala dinner at the Conservative Political Action Conference (CPAC)’s four-day “gathering of visionaries” event, where the former British prime minister Liz Truss is also due to speak.
“Even when what seems like the end isn’t what we’d hoped for, we must thank God and have even more faith that this isn’t yet the end,” he added. “No one shuts the door that he opens – and the door he shuts, no one opens.”
Earlier, in his first post-election interview, Bolsonaro made a series of unsubstantiated claims about election fraud and insisted he received “help from absolutely no one” to flee.
“It was all me,” Bolsonaro told the New York Times, contradicting reports that he was helped by the Trump adviser Jason Miller and Santiago Caputo, a close aide to Argentina’s rightwing president, Javier Milei.
He said he would “take to the grave” the full story of how he had fled Brazil, where he faces federal police investigations for money laundering and corruption. Bolsonaro is a member of congress who has held elected office for more than 20 years but he will lose parliamentary immunity early next year when his term ends, meaning he could then be prosecuted.
Brazilian analysts agree that by skipping the country after an election in which he received 59m votes, Bolsonaro, the son of jailed former president Jair Bolsonaro, abdicated leadership of the opposition and sabotaged his political future.
Thomas Traumann, an author and pundit for the TV network GloboNews, said: “Flávio was foolish enough to throw away the leadership of the opposition that he could have exercised had he stayed in Brazil. But the [Bolsonaro] family is still a player.”
Flávio Bolsonaro’s brother, the former congressman Eduardo Bolsonaro, also lives in self-imposed exile in the US and will have to serve a four-year sentence for coercion if he returns to Brazil. Four other members of the Bolsonaro family were elected to congress in last month’s election, including their brothers Carlos and Jair Renan and stepmother, Michelle Bolsonaro.
Traumann believed it was not inconceivable that Jair Bolsonaro would attempt a political comeback if he managed to negotiate his way out of his 27-year prison sentence for plotting a coup after losing the 2022 election to Lula. However, as things stand, the 71-year-old is banned from running for office until 2060 and must live under house arrest.
Many doubt the Bolsonaro family can continue to control Bolsonarismo, the populist political movement that takes their name, with two key members in exile and one imprisoned.
“[The movement] is mortally wounded because of its mistakes and its crimes,” the political scientist Sérgio Abranches told the newspaper O Globo this week.
Abranches said democratic rightwing politicians now had a chance to “detach” themselves from the Bolsonaros’ anti-democratic movement and break off in a new direction before the next presidential election in 2030.
Flávio Bolsonaro told the New York Times he would “obviously” be a candidate in future elections but said his future lay in the US “at least for now”.
It is unclear where Flávio Bolsonaro, who has been granted a US visa by Trump, will live. His brother Eduardo set up home in Southlake, Texas, after leaving Brazil last year – although some expect him to move after the traditionally conservative state elected the Democrat Gina Hinojosa as governor in this week’s midterms.
In a video posted on CPAC’s social networks before Thursday’s event, Eduardo Bolsonaro played down the risk posed by the “blue tsunami” to their ability to stay in the US. “They [Democrats] will try [to make trouble for us] – but it’s not up to Congress … to revoke visas or citizenships,” he said.
Likening their plight to that of a female asylum seeker fleeing Iran for fear of being killed after refusing to wear a hijab, he added: “I am 100% legal – as is my brother and his family.”

Thomas Traumann, an author and pundit for the TV network GloboNews, said: “Flávio was foolish enough to throw away the leadership of the opposition that he could have exercised had he stayed in Brazil. But the [Bolsonaro] family is still a player.”
Flávio Bolsonaro’s brother, the former congressman Eduardo Bolsonaro, also lives in self-imposed exile in the US and will have to serve a four-year sentence for coercion if he returns to Brazil. Four other members of the Bolsonaro family were elected to congress in last month’s election, including their brothers Carlos and Jair Renan and stepmother, Michelle Bolsonaro.
Traumann believed it was not inconceivable that Jair Bolsonaro would attempt a political comeback if he managed to negotiate his way out of his 27-year prison sentence for plotting a coup after losing the 2022 election to Lula. However, as things stand, the 71-year-old is banned from running for office until 2060 and must live under house arrest.
Many doubt the Bolsonaro family can continue to control Bolsonarismo, the populist political movement that takes their name, with two key members in exile and one imprisoned.
“[The movement] is mortally wounded because of its mistakes and its crimes,” the political scientist Sérgio Abranches told the newspaper O Globo this week.
Abranches said democratic rightwing politicians now had a chance to “detach” themselves from the Bolsonaros’ anti-democratic movement and break off in a new direction before the next presidential election in 2030.
Flávio Bolsonaro told the New York Times he would “obviously” be a candidate in future elections but said his future lay in the US “at least for now”.
It is unclear where Flávio Bolsonaro, who has been granted a US visa by Trump, will live. His brother Eduardo set up home in Southlake, Texas, after leaving Brazil last year – although some expect him to move after the traditionally conservative state elected the Democrat Gina Hinojosa as governor in this week’s midterms.
In a video posted on CPAC’s social networks before Thursday’s event, Eduardo Bolsonaro played down the risk posed by the “blue tsunami” to their ability to stay in the US. “They [Democrats] will try [to make trouble for us] – but it’s not up to Congress … to revoke visas or citizenships,” he said.
Likening their plight to that of a female asylum seeker fleeing Iran for fear of being killed after refusing to wear a hijab, he added: “I am 100% legal – as is my brother and his family.”

title: Employers to be forced to put salaries on job ads, Andy Burnham announces
content_c:
Employers will be forced to publish salaries on job adverts, Andy Burnham has announced, in an effort to empower both employees and jobseekers.
The prime minister said his government would bring in a legal requirement for companies to say what they pay when listing new jobs, which campaigners say will help young people and women in particular achieve more equal pay.
Burnham said the move would help deal with the frustration of applying for a job without knowing the salary, while officials say that publicising pay will help those in work know if they are being paid fairly in comparison with others.
The prime minister said: “Whether you’re a young person starting out or a parent trying to support your family, you should know what a job pays before spending your time and effort applying for it. That’s why we will make it a legal requirement for all employers to say what you pay.
“But breaking down barriers is only one part of the job. We also need businesses to open more doors and give young people the experience and confidence to take that first step into the world of work.”
Paul Nowak, the general secretary of the Trades Union Congress, said: “Anyone who’s searched for a job knows how frustrating it is to read ‘competitive salary’.”
Burnham has spent much of his first few months in power announcing a series of “small fixes” to help improve people’s daily lives, while promising more radical change to come. The changes have included removing VAT from electricity bills, reducing bus fares and a £100 council-tax rebate.
The prime minister is working on a 10-year plan for ending what he calls “40 years of neoliberalism”, which is expected to include more fundamental changes, such as bringing utilities under public control. He said this week the plan’s publication could be delayed until next year, having originally been expected next month.
Ministers first consulted in July on a series of moves to improve how equal pay laws work. That document also proposed greater equality protections for disabled people and ethnic minorities, but ministers have not yet set out their final plans on those points.
They have promised further policy changes to help young people into work in response to a review by the former minister Alan Milburn to be published in the coming weeks.
Recent research by the Chartered Institute of Personnel and Development found less than half of employers always published salaries ranges on job adverts, while less than a fifth always published specific salaries.
Experts say omitting pay details from job adverts makes it harder for young people to know which jobs to apply for, and makes it easier for employers to offer lower pay to some candidates, including women.
The government said 93% of businesses responded positively to the consultation. Ministers have not yet decided exactly what information will have to be published, which size of company will have to comply, or how it will be enforced.

title: Tankers carrying Russian diesel to the US change course
content_c:
Tankers carrying Russian diesel to the US change course
November 6, 2026
Several sanctioned tankers headed for the US carrying Russian diesel are said to have changed course, one toward Brazil and the other into the Mediterranean, according to data from marine data company Kpler and vessel traffic site MarineTraffic.com.
The tankers reportedly departed from the Baltic Sea port of Primorsk last month and had declared their destinations as the US east coast.
This all comes after US President Donald Trump eased sanctions on Russian oil last month, in a deal with with Russian leader Vladimir Putin to secure a large amount of diesel directly to the US at a time when diesel prices have skyrocketed across the country.
The agreement caused shock and drew criticism in Ukraine and Europe. But it also was a logistical challenge, given that sanctions against Russia still remain in place.
It was also widely reported at the time that the amount of diesel in question was a fraction of the US daily demand.
Russia says reports are 'fake'
UK newspaper The Financial Times (FT) reported Wednesday that two of the tankers appeared to have changed their destination and were no longer headed to the United States.
Russian envoy and negotiator Kirill Dmitriev said on Thursday that the US-bound diesel tankers were still on course.
"Fake. Tankers destined for the US continue on course," Dmitriev said on X, linking to the FT story.
Putin's spokesman Dmitry Peskov said detail of shipments were a "commercial" matter that could not be made public.
"All diesel will find its buyers," he added, without elaborating.
A third vessel was still in the North Atlantic headed toward the US but changed its destination from New York to a vague "for orders," without listing an unloading point.
NJ governor threatens 'harsh penalties'
Despite the fact that the US Treasury Department temporarily authorized Russian diesel transactions, New Jersey Governor Mikie Sherrill warned port and terminal operators to turn away ships carrying the fuel.
In a letter earlier this week, she warned that "any effort to profit from the illegal trade in Russian fuel will be met with harsh penalties.”
Sherrill accused the Trump administration of lacking authority in overriding the import ban enacted by Congress more than four years ago.
She said New Jersey would act to prevent state facilities and companies from handling Russian fuel.
In a letter dated October 27, Connecticut Senator Richard Blumenthal warned shipping companies against violating US sanctions forbidding imports of Russian fuel.
"No president can unilaterally override a statute. Trump's license will not absolve you of legal and moral accountability," the letter read.
description: Despite an ostensible deal between Donald Trump and Vladimir Putin to bring diesel to the US, tankers are reportedly unable to dock due to existing sanctions.

title: Papst Leo XIV. beginnt Südamerika-Reise in Uruguay
content_c:
Papst Leo XIV. in Südamerika Zu Gast nicht nur bei Freunden
Drei Länder in elf Tagen: In Uruguay beginnt Papst Leo XIV. heute seine Südamerika-Reise. Auf ihn warten auch die Heimat seines Vorgängers und ein Wiedersehen mit der eigenen Vergangenheit.
Hoch zu Ross, mit der typischen Gaucho-Mütze auf dem Kopf und ihren Kindern mit im Sattel - so ziehen sie über die sanften Hügel und sattgrünen Weiden der Pampa: Wie jedes Jahr Anfang November begeben sich Gläubige aus Uruguays Hinterland auf einen Pilgerritt zu Ehren der Heiligen Jungfrau der Dreiunddreißig, Uruguays Schutzpatronin.
"Es geht auch darum, unsere Kultur zu pflegen - beim Miteinander, beim Lagerfeuer, beim gemeinsamen Weg den Glauben neu zu entdecken", sagt Padre Leonardo Risso, der die Wallfahrt zu Pferde organisiert. "Wir sind ein kleines Land, in dem nur eine Minderheit gläubig und praktizierend ist. Die katholische Kirche ist hier eine Minderheit."
Ein Grund: Kirche und Staat wurden in Uruguay bereits im frühen 20. Jahrhundert klar getrennt. Weihnachten heißt hier "Familientag", Ostern "Reisewoche". Umso mehr freut sich Gaucho-Padre Risso, dass er zum Abschluss der Wallfahrt bei der Messe in der Basilika von Florida einen besonderen Gast begrüßen darf: Papst Leo XIV., der in Uruguay seine elftägige Südamerika-Reise startet. "Ich finde es gut, dass er seine Reise hier beginnt - in einem Land, das einen Impuls braucht", sagt Risso. "Es ist wie eine Botschaft der Freude, die hier alle brauchen."
Ein diplomatisch heikler Besuch in Argentinien
Der Auftakt im laizistischsten Staat Lateinamerikas dürfte der einfachste Besuch für das Kirchenoberhaupt werden. Im Anschluss reist er nach Argentinien, das Heimatland seines Vorgängers Franziskus. Der hatte Argentinien aber trotz zahlreicher Einladungen nie als Papst besucht - wohl auch, weil er vermeiden wollte, dass seine Anwesenheit in einem polarisierten Land politisch vereinnahmt werde.
Bei seinen Landsleuten sorgte das für Frust, umso größer nun die Erwartungen. Denn Papst Leo besucht Argentinien in einem Moment, in dem die Schere zwischen Arm und Reich immer weiter auseinandergeht. Der radikale Sparkurs des libertären Präsidenten Javier Milei hat viele Menschen gesellschaftlich an den Rand gedrängt. Der Besuch von Leo, der wie Franziskus für eine Kirche an der Seite der Armen steht, ist für Milei diplomatisch heikel, glaubt der Kirchenexperte und Anthropologe Pablo Sernan:
                
                
                Für die Regierung ist dieser Besuch nicht gerade angenehm. Es handelt sich um einen Papst, der soziale Gerechtigkeit predigt - während der Präsident soziale Gerechtigkeit für eine Abartigkeit hält. Ein Aufeinanderprallen gegensätzlicher Grundannahmen ist unvermeidlich.
Eine Art Heimkehr nach Peru
In Peru, der letzten Station seiner Reise, trifft der Papst auf eine stark polarisierte Gesellschaft, wie der nur hauchdünne Wahlsieg von Präsidentin Keiko Fujimori gezeigt hat. Gleichzeitig ist es für ihn ein Heimkehren: Fast 21 Jahren war Robert Francis Prevost, wie der Papst mit bürgerlichem Namen heißt, in Peru als Missionar und Bischof von Chiclayo tätig
Für die Peruaner ist er schlichtweg "ihr" Papst. Das Land sei wie auf Dopamin, umso mehr noch die Menschen in Chiclayo, seiner einstigen Wirkungsstätte, sagt die Journalistin Pau Ugaz. Trotzdem sei es auch in Peru kein einfacher Besuch:
                
                
                Man will keine Unruhe, alles soll friedlich bleiben. Das ist es, was der konservative Flügel vermitteln möchte: ein politisch stabiles Peru, in dem es keinerlei Probleme gibt. Alles soll sozusagen im 'Papst-Modus' ablaufen, in einer Art 'Dopamin-Modus'. Doch das spiegelt die Persönlichkeit von León XIV. keineswegs wider, oder?
Gespräche mit Missbrauchsopfern angekündigt
Der Papst hat sich in seiner Zeit als Bischof für soziale Verantwortung in einem Staat eingesetzt, der für viele Menschen kaum präsent ist: Er arbeitete mit Migranten, unterstützte bei Naturkatastrophen und stellte sich hinter Journalisten wie Ugaz, die zu kirchliche Machtstrukturen und Missbrauch recherchierten. Auch für diese Reise sind Gespräche mit Missbrauchsopfern angekündigt - und Treffen mit Indigenen aus abgelegenen Amazonas-Gebieten.
Von der Pampa über die Anden bis an den Pazifik: So unterschiedlich die Stationen in Südamerika sein mögen, sie verbindet die Hoffnung, der Pontifex möge als Brückenbauer einen Beitrag leisten, um Gräben und gesellschaftliche Spaltungen zu überwinden.
