title: Most Europeans want action to tackle climate crisis but not at any cost, poll shows
content_c:
Europeans believe human-made climate change is real, a survey has shown, with most feeling action must be taken soon – as long as they do not have to sacrifice too much to achieve it.
The YouGov poll of six European countries showed between 69% (Germany) and 80% (France) of respondents believed the climate was changing, with few (1%-4%) denying it and 14-20% believing it was changing, but not as a result of human activity.
Europe is the world’s fastest-warming continent and scientists say human-driven climate breakdown through the burning of fossil fuels is increasing the frequency and intensity of heatwaves, droughts, wildfires and destructive storms.
Days before the Cop31 climate conference in Turkey, the polling showed vast majorities (79-89%) in Denmark, France, Germany, Italy, Spain and the UK thought countries would combat the crisis more effectively by working internationally.
Those in the EU were more likely to say that climate action decisions should be made at EU rather than national level, a feeling shared by 50-54% of respondents in France, Italy and Germany as well as 61% in Denmark and 64% in Spain.
Majorities of between 65% and 83% in each country surveyed said they were worried about the climate crisis, including 23%-42% who were “very worried”. YouGov noted an uptick in concern during this summer’s heatwaves.
In April, 74% of respondents in France said they were worried about the climate crisis but that figure was up to 83% by mid-August and still at that level last month.
The number of French people who were “very worried” about climate change also rose, from 28% in April to a record high of 42% in August, a level it held last month. Concern in other countries spiked in August but has since dipped.
In Germany, for example, the number very concerned rose from 27% in April to 40% in August but has now fallen back to 31%. Concern remained relatively stable in Denmark, at 66%-69% “worried” and 20%-23% “very worried”.
Across the six countries surveyed, respondents mostly (45%-63%) thought it was not too late to avert the worst impacts of the climate crisis but that it would require a drastic change in approach. Only 11%-24% believed it was already too late.
Between 9% and 20% said they thought current measures would be enough to prevent the most serious impacts. But in terms of what climate actions had support, those not directly affecting people’s lives were the most popular.
Measures such as planting more trees, subsidising energy efficiency, banning single-use plastics and taxing big emitters were all favoured, while increasing fuel duty, limiting meat and dairy, taxing air fares and banning new petrol and diesel cars were opposed.
A similar pattern emerged when respondents were asked what steps they would be prepared to take: cheap and easy actions such as creating green space at home and eating only seasonal fruit and vegetables were popular, but not shopping exclusively secondhand or paying more for flights.

title: Czech arms makers set sights on space defense in bid to sustain Ukraine-driven arms boom
content_c:
Czech arms makers look spaceward in bid to sustain Ukraine-driven boom
November 6, 2026
The Czechoslovak Group (CSG) arms maker announced in mid-October that it has acquired a stake in Canadian space technology manufacturer MDA Space.
This space mission is part of the company's bid to continue riding the boom that has transformed its fortunes in recent years.
When it listed on the Amsterdam Stock Exchange earlier this year, CSG soared to become the most valuable company in Central and Eastern Europe, with a market capitalization of €14.6 billion ($16.4 billion), propelling its owner, Michal Strnad, to the top of the region's rich list.
From 90s startup to major European player
CSG began life as a 1990s startup, selling military surplus amid the collapse of the Warsaw Pact, the military alliance between the Soviet Union and Europe's socialist Eastern Bloc nations, which was founded in 1955 and disbanded in 1991.
It has since grown to become the second-largest producer of ammunition in Europe after Germany's Rheinmetall and now produces across Europe and in the US.
The impact of the war in Ukraine
The main driver of the company's rising fortunes has been Russia's war in Ukraine, which has driven a dramatic boom across the Czech defense industry as a whole.
In 2021, the sector's exports totaled €600 million. In 2025, these exports had expanded to €4.7 billion, powered by orders placed by Kyiv and its European allies.
By the end of that year, European states had procured approximately €11 billion worth of military support for Ukraine from Czech defense firms.
Orders to the value of roughly €4 billion have arrived via the Czech Ammunition Initiative, a program that coordinates the transfer of artillery shells to Ukraine.
Amid the avalanche of orders sparked by Russia's full-scale invasion of Ukraine in 2022, CSG and Czech peers such as STV, Colt CZ and PBS have been busy expanding production to pump out military vehicles and planes, guns, grenades, shells and bullets.
Historical link
"The war in Ukraine, particularly in its early stages, was especially well suited to Czech firms," Krzysytof Debiec of the Centre for Eastern Studies (OSW) told DW.
Debiec says that this was largely due to the major role that the former Czechoslovakia played in supplying Warsaw Pact countries.
"Specialization in the production of ammunition — including Soviet calibers — the repair of Soviet-era equipment and the manufacture of relatively unsophisticated systems that could be rapidly introduced and were compatible with the Ukrainian army's existing stocks," have all been key, he explained.
At the same time, European states eyeing the threat from the east and broader geopolitical instability are boosting their own defense budgets.
"The shift in US policies vis-a-vis NATO is forcing European nations to increase their defense spending dramatically, and that's another factor" in the Czech defense industry boom, Jan Jires, a former deputy defense minister and now a senior advisor at the International Institute for Strategic Studies, told DW.
Export dependence
However, since launching on the stock exchange, CSG's share price has performed erratically, illustrating the shifting sands on which Czechia's booming defense industry now stands.
The government in Prague has responded to the sector's surge by transferring the defense industry portfolio from the Ministry of Defense to the Ministry of Industry and Trade to align its growing role in exports with national economic and trade policy.
At the same time, the populist ruling coalition that took power a year ago is made up of parties that have either promised to lower support for Ukraine or — in the case of the far-right Freedom and Direct Democracy party (SPD) — are openly pro-Russian.
As a result, the coalition has halted contributions to the Czech Ammunition Initiative and is dragging its feet on raising defense spending to meet NATO targets.
This only limits an already small domestic market, leaving the industry dependent on exports for about 90% of its revenue — the vast bulk of which is still linked to Ukraine — and lacking a stable base for expansion.
"The Czech industry has outgrown the country's financial means," said Jires. "Unlike German, French or British companies, Czech manufacturers cannot rely on domestic demand to make them globally relevant."
What the future holds
Increased global defense spending looks set to continue, but an end to Russia's war in Ukraine, a change in US foreign policy or a calmer geopolitical environment would hit Czech arms manufacturers hard. For this reason, they must ponder what the future of war, and its funding, might look like.
The conflict in Ukraine offers some indicators, having become increasingly focused on swarms of drones and a technological race between Kyiv and Moscow to improve the performance of the unmanned aircraft.
Major questions must now be asked regarding "the size and role of the military, how it is equipped, what should be purchased and when new weaponry can arrive" Andor Sandor, a defense analyst and former commander of Czechia's Military Intelligence Service, told DW.
For a company like CSG, for which bullets and shells currently account for around 60% of sales, these are vital questions.
"Czech companies — many of which still focus on relatively unsophisticated military production — must invest more in innovative manufacturing," said Debiec, who notes that most are well aware of the challenge. "They have reinvested their extraordinary profits and are already more technologically advanced and diversified in their production than they were in 2022."
Space mission
CSG's acquisition of MDA Space is part of such efforts.
The company, which already held interests in British and German space technology companies, pointed to the close link between the space and defense industries when it announced the deal.
Noting that global government spending on space defense accelerated to €65.83 billion last year, CSG estimates that the overall space economy will triple in size to €1.6 trillion over the next decade.
Developing capabilities in space is "a natural extension" of its activities, the company stated, noting plans for further development in the segment, including a "dedicated space team."
To power such missions, Czech defense companies must make sure they're in a position to tap into funds for defense and space under the next EU budget, which could rise as high as €130 billion, said Jires.
"If they fail to do so, and all this money is grabbed by German, French and Italian companies," he warned, "Czech manufacturers may miss the opportunity to truly scale-up."
description: Czech arms makers have thrived on demand linked to the war in Ukraine. To sustain their growth, they need to look beyond ammunition and toward new technologies — and even space.

title: Berlin: Linke fordert Vanessa Emde auf, Mandat zurückzugeben
content_c:
Umstrittene Abgeordnete Berliner Linke fordert Mandatsverzicht von Emde
Die Parteiführung der Berliner Linken hat die Abgeordnete Vanessa Emde aufgefordert, ihr Mandat zurückzugeben. Eine entsprechende Stellungnahme des Landesvorstandes liegt dem SPIEGEL vor.
»Wir vertrauen ihr nicht mehr«, erklärte der Linke-Landesvorstand. Emde habe mehrfach gegen die Mandatsträgervereinbarung verstoßen: »Sie hat die gemeinsame Fraktionserklärung der Abgeordneten öffentlich infrage gestellt, ist auf einer Kundgebung gegen unsere Partei aufgetreten, statt auf unserem Parteitag als gewählte Delegierte für ihre Position zu streiten.« Außerdem habe sie sich bis heute nicht von denen distanziert, die den 7. Oktober als legitimen Widerstand feiern.
Ob Emde ihr Mandat tatsächlich zurückgibt, ist offen. Tut sie es nicht, könnte sie aus der Linkefraktion im Berliner Abgeordnetenhaus ausgeschlossen werden.
Demo gegen eigene Partei
Emde war am 20. September neu ins Landesparlament gewählt worden. Sie holte mit einem Erststimmenergebnis von 46,2 Prozent ein Direktmandat in ihrem Wahlkreis in Neukölln. Die Linkenpolitikerin steht wegen Äußerungen zum Nahostkonflikt schon länger in der Kritik, sie erschwert mit ihren Äußerungen seit Wochen den Weg zu einer Regierungsbildung in Berlin. Emde wird unter anderem vorgeworfen, das Existenzrecht Israels in Zweifel zu ziehen. Teil des Koalitionsvertrags soll eine gemeinsame Erklärung von Linken, Grünen und SPD werden, auf die sich die Parteien schon vor Beginn der Sondierungen geeinigt haben. Darin stehen Bekenntnisse zum Schutz jüdischen Lebens in Berlin, zum Existenzrecht Israels und zu einer Zweistaatenlösung, die sowohl Israels Sicherheit als auch die Selbstbestimmung der Palästinenser ermöglichen soll. Emde argumentiert allerdings, Staaten hätten – anders als Menschen – kein Existenzrecht.
Am vergangenen Wochenende demonstrierte Emde am Rande eines Linken-Parteitages gegen ihre eigene Parteiführung. Dabei erklärte sie sich solidarisch mit einem bekannten propalästinensischen Aktivisten und mutmaßlichen Terrorbefürworter.
Emde soll sich entschuldigen
Der Landesvorstand schreibt: »Es reicht, genug ist genug. Vanessa Emde hat eine Woche Zeit, zu uns zurückzukehren.« Dazu solle sie ihre Instagram-Beiträge löschen, sich für ihren Auftritt am Rande des Parteitags entschuldigen und eine konstruktive Zusammenarbeit auf Grundlage der Linken-Beschlüsse zusagen. Das Mandat sei keine »Ich-AG«, die Berliner Linke fasse Beschlüsse gemeinsam – niemand solle die eigene Partei angreifbar machen.
»Unsere Haltung bleibt klar: Solidarität mit den Palästinenserinnen und Palästinensern, Einsatz für einen eigenen Staat und gleiche Rechte für alle Menschen«, heißt es in der Stellungnahme. »Zugleich treten wir entschieden gegen Antisemitismus ein und stehen aus historischer Verantwortung für das Existenzrecht Israels. Diese Grundlage gilt für alle, die in unserem Namen sprechen.«
Zuletzt hatte sich Linkenpolitiker Gregor Gysi für einen Fraktionsausschluss der umstrittenen Abgeordneten ausgesprochen. »Ich hoffe, dass wir sie ausschließen«, sagte Gysi im Podcast des »Bild«-Journalisten Paul Ronzheimer. Bislang wurde diese Entscheidung mehrfach vertagt.
Anmerkung der Redaktion: In einer früheren Version wurde der Linkenparteitag falsch verortet, wir haben den Fehler korrigiert.
description: Der Konflikt um Vanessa Emde erschwert die Koalitionsgespräche in Berlin. Nun hat die Partei sie gedrängt, ihren Posten aufzugeben – das Mandat sei keine »Ich-AG«. Hintergrund sind ihre Positionen zum Nahostkonflikt.

Teil des Koalitionsvertrags soll eine gemeinsame Erklärung von Linken, Grünen und SPD werden, auf die sich die Parteien schon vor Beginn der Sondierungen geeinigt haben. Darin stehen Bekenntnisse zum Schutz jüdischen Lebens in Berlin, zum Existenzrecht Israels und zu einer Zweistaatenlösung, die sowohl Israels Sicherheit als auch die Selbstbestimmung der Palästinenser ermöglichen soll. Emde argumentiert allerdings, Staaten hätten – anders als Menschen – kein Existenzrecht.
Am vergangenen Wochenende demonstrierte Emde am Rande eines Linken-Parteitages gegen ihre eigene Parteiführung. Dabei erklärte sie sich solidarisch mit einem bekannten propalästinensischen Aktivisten und mutmaßlichen Terrorbefürworter.
Emde soll sich entschuldigen
Der Landesvorstand schreibt: »Es reicht, genug ist genug. Vanessa Emde hat eine Woche Zeit, zu uns zurückzukehren.« Dazu solle sie ihre Instagram-Beiträge löschen, sich für ihren Auftritt am Rande des Parteitags entschuldigen und eine konstruktive Zusammenarbeit auf Grundlage der Linken-Beschlüsse zusagen. Das Mandat sei keine »Ich-AG«, die Berliner Linke fasse Beschlüsse gemeinsam – niemand solle die eigene Partei angreifbar machen.
»Unsere Haltung bleibt klar: Solidarität mit den Palästinenserinnen und Palästinensern, Einsatz für einen eigenen Staat und gleiche Rechte für alle Menschen«, heißt es in der Stellungnahme. »Zugleich treten wir entschieden gegen Antisemitismus ein und stehen aus historischer Verantwortung für das Existenzrecht Israels. Diese Grundlage gilt für alle, die in unserem Namen sprechen.«
Zuletzt hatte sich Linkenpolitiker Gregor Gysi für einen Fraktionsausschluss der umstrittenen Abgeordneten ausgesprochen. »Ich hoffe, dass wir sie ausschließen«, sagte Gysi im Podcast des »Bild«-Journalisten Paul Ronzheimer. Bislang wurde diese Entscheidung mehrfach vertagt.
Anmerkung der Redaktion: In einer früheren Version wurde der Linkenparteitag falsch verortet, wir haben den Fehler korrigiert.

title: Ilse Aigner soll laut ARD-Informationen Bundespräsidentin werden
content_c:
Steinmeier-Nachfolge Union will Aigner als Bundespräsidentin
Sie wäre dort die erste Frau: Laut ARD-Hauptstadtstudio werden CDU und CSU Ilse Aigner als Kandidatin für das Amt der Bundespräsidentin vorschlagen. Gemeinsam mit der SPD hätten sie in der Bundesversammlung eine Mehrheit.
Die Unionsparteien sind sich einig, dass sie die CSU-Politikerin Ilse Aigner als Bundespräsidentin vorschlagen wollen. Das erfuhr das ARD-Hauptstadtstudio. Ihre Nominierung soll am Montag bekannt gegeben werden. Zuerst hatten die Süddeutsche Zeitung und der Spiegel darüber berichtet.
Die formelle Entscheidung sollen CDU-Präsidium und -Vorstand am Montag treffen. Schon am Sonntagabend trifft Bundeskanzler und CDU-Chef Friedrich Merz die Mitglieder des Präsidiums zu einem Abendessen. CSU-Chef Markus Söder hatte Aigner schon im April ins Spiel gebracht.
Klare Mehrheit in Bundesversammlung
Das neue deutsche Staatsoberhaupt wird von der Bundesversammlung am 30. Januar gewählt. Frank-Walter Steinmeier (SPD) scheidet dann nach zehn Jahren aus dem Amt.
Der Versammlung gehören neben den 630 Bundestagsabgeordneten ebenso viele Wahlleute aus den Ländern an. Union und SPD haben dort eine Mehrheit von etwa 50 Stimmen. Es gilt als wahrscheinlich, dass Merz versucht, die Grünen einzubinden.
Die AfD will einen eigenen Kandidaten aufstellen. Das gilt wegen der Mehrheitsverhältnisse aber als aussichtslos.
Merz blieb zurückhaltend
Merz hatte sich bislang nicht öffentlich geäußert, ob er die 61-Jährige unterstützt. Er legte sich lediglich fest, dass eine Frau ins höchste Staatsamt gewählt werden soll. Merz hatte klargemacht, dass er das Vorschlagsrecht bei der CDU sieht - sie ist die stärkste Kraft in der Bundesversammlung.
In den vergangenen Tagen hatten sich immer mehr CDU-Landeschefs für Aigner ausgesprochen. Auch Unions-Fraktionschef Thorsten Frei äußerte sich positiv über sie.
Klingbeil lobt "wahnsinnig integrative Kraft"
SPD-Chef Lars Klingbeil sagte, wenn die Union sich für Aigner ausspreche, "dann kann ich nur für die SPD sagen, dann würden wir das begrüßen und unterstützen". Aigner habe "eine wahnsinnig integrative Kraft", die Deutschland gerade in diesen Zeiten brauche: "Die ist eine sehr volksnahe Politikerin, die redet mit den Menschen auf Augenhöhe, das ist total wichtig".
Auch SPD-Bundestagsfraktionschef Matthias Miersch und einzelne SPD-Ministerpräsidenten sprachen sich schon für Aigner aus.
Grüne zeigen sich ebenfalls offen
Die Grünen zeigten ebenfalls Sympathien für Aigner. "Sie ist in ihren bisherigen politischen Ämtern stets nahbar und zugewandt aufgetreten", sagte Fraktionschefin Britta Haßelmann. "Wir Grünen halten es für angemessen und richtig, dass erstmals nach 75 Jahren eine Frau das höchste Amt im Staat bekleidet. Die Zeit ist reif dafür." Es brauche in diesen Zeiten ein Staatsoberhaupt, das das Land zusammenführen könne.
Zugleich kritisierte die Co-Fraktionschefin der Grünen die Kandidatensuche der Union. Seit Wochen rede die Republik über einen Vorschlag nach dem anderen für das Amt. "Die unprofessionelle Findungssuche der Union und von Friedrich Merz ist dieses Amtes unwürdig. Wie kann man einen Prozess derart verstolpern?"
Reichinnek spricht von "Versorgungsposten"
Linksfraktionschefin Heidi Reichinnek kritisierte, es wäre sinnvoller gewesen, "eine überparteiliche Kandidatur anzubieten, von der sich breite Teile der Bevölkerung repräsentiert fühlen". Der Augsburger Allgemeinen sagte sie, "dass das Amt des Bundespräsidenten immer wieder als Versorgungsposten zwischen den Unionsparteien und der SPD hin- und hergeschoben wird, wird der Rolle dieses Amtes nicht gerecht".
Aigner wäre erste Frau an der Staatsspitze
Die 61-Jährige wäre nach zwölf Männern die erste Frau an der Staatsspitze der Bundesrepublik. Sie hätte zudem als erstes Staatsoberhaupt nicht studiert und wäre die erste ledige Person in dem Amt. Bislang haben neun Frauen erfolglos versucht, Bundespräsidentin zu werden.
Aigner ist seit 2018 Präsidentin des bayerischen Landtags. Schon bei ihrer ersten Wahl erzielte sie dort mit 198 von 205 Stimmen eine überwältigende Mehrheit. Im Kabinett von Kanzlerin Angela Merkel war sie zuvor von 2008 bis 2013 Bundeslandwirtschaftsministerin gewesen.
Eine Systemelektrikerin für Hubschrauber
Aigner stammt aus dem oberbayrischen Feldkirchen-Westerham. Nach der Mittleren Reife 1981 ließ sie sich zur Radio- und Fernsehtechnikerin ausbilden. Später bildete sie sich zur Systemelektrikerin für Hubschrauber weiter.
"Ungeklärte Familienverhältnisse" - sie ist nicht verheiratet - waren nach Aigners Angaben ein Grund dafür, dass die CSU sie 1993 nicht zur Bürgermeisterkandidatin ihrer Heimatgemeinde machte. Nach einer kurzen Zeit im Landtag ab 1994 sprang Aigner für einen ausgefallenen CSU-Direktkandidaten bei der Bundestagswahl 1998 ein und gewann das Mandat.
Aigner hat schwere Krankheiten hinter sich. Im Jugendalter wurde bei ihr ein Tumor im Rücken diagnostiziert. Durch eine Operation entging sie einer drohenden Querschnittslähmung. Als Ministerin überwand sie Schilddrüsenkrebs mit einer Strahlentherapie.
"Schicksalsgemeinschaft mit Söder"
Mit CSU-Chef und dem bayerischen Ministerpräsidenten Markus Söder verbinde sie eine "Schicksalsgemeinschaft", sagte Aigner einmal. Beide zogen gleichzeitig in den Landtag ein, waren Kollegen im Landesvorstand der Jungen Union und im Kabinett von Horst Seehofer. Den Wettstreit um Seehofers Nachfolge verlor sie 2018 gegen Söder.
An seiner Unterstützung für eine Bundespräsidentin Aigner hatte Söder seit einem halben Jahr keinen Zweifel mehr gelassen. "Wenn sie möchte, hat sie meine volle Sympathie und Unterstützung", sagte er im April. Ende Oktober nutzte er den CSU-Parteitag, um für sie zu werben.
Nach Einschätzung von ARD-Korrespondent Philip Kuntschner setzte sich Söder bei der Kandidatensuche gegen Merz durch. Seine Chancen, eines Tages selbst Kanzler zu werden, seien dadurch aber geschmälert.

title: Атака на Київ: серед трьох постраждалих є дитина (фото)
content_c:
Атака на Київ: серед трьох постраждалих є дитина (фото)
У Солом’янському районі рятувальники зафіксували руйнування будівель і загасили пожежу вантажівки та нежитлової споруди.
У ніч проти 7 листопада внаслідок російської атаки на Київ постраждали троє людей, серед них дитина. У Солом’янському районі пошкоджені житлові будинки та будівля на території дитячого садка.
Про це повідомила Державна служба України з надзвичайних ситуацій.
За однією з адрес частково зруйновано фасад першого поверху житлової п’ятиповерхівки. Загоряння не виникло, ніхто там не постраждав.
Ще за трьома адресами вибухова хвиля вибила вікна в п’ятиповерхових будинках. Одна людина травмувалася.
Атака на Київ: серед трьох постраждалих є дитина (фото) (11 фото)
Також рятувальники зафіксували руйнування двоповерхової будівлі на території дитсадка. На іншій локації горіли припаркована вантажівка та нежитлова будівля. Пожежу ліквідували.
За ще двома адресами постраждали двоє людей, зокрема дитина.
Раніше Київська міська військова адміністрація повідомляла про двох постраждалих унаслідок атаки.
Раніше міський голова Віталій Кличко повідомив про влучання уламків у житлову п’ятиповерхівку в Солом’янському районі. За іншою адресою вибухова хвиля пошкодила вікна ще одного п’ятиповерхового будинку.

title: Пожар и взрывы в Орле: что известно
content_c:
Местные жители сообщают о вероятной ракетной атаке на район промышленного кластера «Протон».
В российском Орле прогремели семь взрывов. Местные жители сообщают о вероятной ракетной атаке на район промышленного кластера «Протон». Ранее, 23 октября, ракеты уже поразили завод «Протон-Электротекс» в этом городе. По данным Генерального штаба ВСУ, тогда был уничтожен основной цех по производству микросхем. Также жители сообщают о пожаре, отмечает мониторинговый канал Exilenova+.
Кластер «Протон» объединяет два завода электронной промышленности: один производит оптоэлектронику, другой — силовые полупроводники. Информация о цели пока предварительная.
По данным Главного управления разведки Министерства обороны Украины, завод «Протон» выпускает оптоэлектронное оборудование по полному циклу, от кристаллов до готовой продукции. Среди его изделий — диодный модуль для авиационной ракеты С-71К «Ковер», переключатель-инвертор для «Искандер-М» и микросхемы для зенитного комплекса «Панцирь-С1». В сентябре 2025 года Великобритания внесла предприятие в санкционный список.

title: Клименко: фігуранти справи "Карфаген" зі мною не спілкувалися, не було людей, через яких могли тиснути
content_c:
Секретар Ради національної безпеки і оборони (РНБО) України Ігор Клименко заявив, що був вкрай здивований фігуруванням свого прізвища на плівках НАБУ щодо операції "Карфаген" і запевнив, що ніхто з ним не спілкувався зі злочинної організації, а також не знає, хто на нього хотів вплинути.
"Дивіться, до мене ніхто взагалі не підходив. Таких розмов у мене ні з ким не було. Тиснути по наркотикам, і по постанові Кабміну, те, що вони мали на увазі – ну, потиснули, бачите, як? Постанова є, U420 – немає", – сказав він на зустрічі із журналістами у п'ятницю, передає кореспондент "Інтерфакс-Україна".
Відповідаючи на уточнююче питання щодо людей в оточенні Клименка, які могли б на нього впливати, він запевнив, що "таких людей не було".
"Я не знаю, про кого йде мова взагалі, тому що немає таких, які на мене могли тиснути. Більше того, навіть не з мого близького оточення, навіть в дальньому оточенні, які могли хтось на мене повпливати, таких людей не було", – зазначив Клименко.
Говорячи про людей в оточенні екс-міністра внутрішніх справ, через яких представники злочинної групи якимось чином хотіли тиснути, Клименко додав, що "Так, було б цікаво, хто на мене хотів повпливати".
На питання, чи вбачає він появу свого прізвища у плівках НАБУ елементом тиску, він відповів: "Не хотів би відповідати на це запитання".
Чи можуть плівки використовуватися для тиску на нього, як на секретаря РНБО, Клименко сказав, що "гіпотетично – можуть".
"Чи в цьому випадку? Не впевнений", – додав він.
Крім того, Клименко заявив, що для нього здивуванням почути фігурування свого прізвища на записах НАБУ, які були оприлюднені?
"Я офігів, чесно. Ну, дивіться, я знаю, що на плівках, оприлюднених у квітні, була історія мене зняти. Це було, але це не дуже привернуло увагу. Хімпром створили мережу телеграм-каналів і новинних сайтів, де вони публікували всякі фейки, і на плівках чути, де Мексиканець говорить, що там інформація ось вийшла, так давайте на фоні знову на них вийдемо і сторгуємося. Тобто вони використовували такі інформаційні бомби, рознести, щоб посадовців репутаційно підбивати в цьому інформаційному шумі. Це був елемент тиску", – заявив секретар РНБО.
Також Клименко висловив сподівання, що "Мексиканця" – засновника та керівника наркосиндикату "Хімпром" Єгора Буркіна (Єгора Левченка), вдасться знайти і повернути в Україну.
"Підозри. Звичайно. У квітні це було озвучено. І зараз ще нові підозри. Я надіюсь, що те, що пообіцяв Поклад (глава СБУ Олександр Поклад – ІФ-У), провести його сюди, надіюсь, що він це реалізує. Його треба повернути. Мексиканця потрібно знайти, повернути сюди, засудити однозначно", – підкреслив він.
Раніше керівник підрозділу детективів Національного антикорупційного бюро (НАБУ) Олександр Абакумов заявив, що матеріали справи щодо операції "Карфаген" свідчать, що підозрювані не спілкувалися із Ігорем Клименком під час перебування його на посаді глави МВС щодо вирішення питання безперешкодного продажу наркотичних засобів.
У програмі "УП. чат", відео якого розміщено на ютюб-каналі "Української правди", Абакумов коментує зафіксоване на відео НАБУ із матеріалами негласних слідчих (розшукових) дій (НСРД) обговорення фігурантами спроби підкупу міністра внутрішніх справ Ігоря Клименка наступним чином: "Прізвище міністра (Клименка) дійсно обговорював керівник "Хімпрому" як людини, через яку він хотів би вирішити питання. Він бачив шлях вирішення свого питання, пов'язаного із безперешкодним продажем наркотичних засобів… через міністра, тому що він вважав, що міністр може не вживати заходів щодо заборони формул цього наркотичного засобу".
Як повідомлялося, антикорупційні органи в межах операції "Карфаген" викрили злочинну організацію, учасники якої налагодили систематичне надання неправомірної вигоди високопосадовцям правоохоронних органів за безперешкодну діяльність шахрайських кол-центрів та інших незаконних бізнесів.
До складу злочинної організації було залучено щонайменше 12 осіб.
В повідомленні САП розміщено відеоматеріали НСРД, в якому уточнюється, що до складу злочинної групи входили: засновник і керівник групи – тричі засуджений "Кримінал", керівник наркокартелю "Хімпром", громадянин РФ "Мексиканець", підлеглі "Кримінала" – "Боксер" та "Паша". За прикриття діяльності кол-центрів, як наголошується у відео, відповідав один із керівників департаменту стратегічних розслідувань Нацполіції "Прайс".
"Акім" – високопосадовець СБУ, генерал-майор, що забезпечував захист від уваги своїх колег", – йдеться у відеоролику НАБУ.
За даними із відкритих джерел, "Мексиканець" – засновник та керівник наркосиндикату "Хімпром" Єгор Буркін, відомий також як Єгор Левченко, громадянин РФ та України, перебуває в розшуку в Україні з 2019 року, проти нього запроваджено персональні санкції.
"Хімпром" – транснаціональне злочинне угруповання, займається виробництвом та збутом синтетичних наркотиків, організацією роботи шахрайських колцентрів.
Андрій Осіпов, "Кримінал", є ключовою фігурою у нових матеріалах операції "Карфаген". За словами прокурора САП Миколи Карася, Осіпов перебуває під вартою з липня 2026 року у іншій справі.
Серед підозрюваних у справі: перший заступник начальника департаменту захисту національної державності Служби безпеки України генерал Сергій Дука ("Акім"), вже звільнений з посади, Олександр Дем'янчук ("Консультант") – заступник начальника відділу Управління карного розшуку Головного управління Національної поліції в Київській області, перший заступник начальника Департаменту стратегічних розслідувань Національної поліції України Володимир Ценов (його ВАКС взяв під варту із альтернативою застави в 15 млн грн), Віталія Рибалка, відомий як "Боксер" (ВАКС узяв під варту без права внесення застави).

title: The young Somali woman changing how the world sees Mogadishu
content_c:
The young Somali woman changing how the world sees Mogadishu
- Published
As the sun rises over the Indian Ocean, waves lap onto the golden sands while palm fronds rustle in the cool sea breeze. Welcome to... Mogadishu.
This is the image that one young Somali woman wants the world to have of her home city - in contrast to the one of suicide attacks and young men wielding AK-47s that many people currently associate with Somalia's capital.
Sucdi Abdul Fattah Abdul Khader is among a growing number of local guides taking visitors beyond the headlines to explore Mogadishu's beauty spots, historic sites and culture.
Her favourite spot is Jazeera beach, where visitors can enjoy the sea before heading to nearby sand dunes.
"It's one of the tourist attractions where we bring our guests. It's a nice place," says the 23-year-old.
The dunes, she adds, remind some visitors of the Sahara.
But her tours are about more than scenic views. She also takes visitors to the fish market, where they discover the variety of marine life available along Somalia's extensive coastline and to parts of the city that reflect its history as a busy Indian Ocean trading centre, with the influences of both its Ottoman and Italian former rulers.
Visitors can also sample Somali food, including camel meat, samosas and traditional tea.
Sucdi says many arrive in the city with expectations shaped by years of hearing about the insecurity.
"Mostly, they are surprised by how beautiful the country is and how welcoming people are," she says.
At the fish market, she says, visitors are particularly impressed by the variety of fish species.
Guiding tours runs in Sucdi's family. Her father worked in the profession for over three decades, taking journalists, photographers and visitors from different countries around Somalia.
He introduced her to the business nearly three years ago.
"I started this job as a hobby, but it has become something that I like and am passionate about," she says.
She now works alongside her father and a team of guides, building on his experience while using social media to reach a wider audience.
She shares videos of her tours on TikTok, offering people outside Somalia a glimpse of places they may never have imagined visiting.
She is also considering producing content in English to reach audiences who do not speak Somali.
Tourism remains a relatively new field in Somalia, she says, with only a handful working as guides in Mogadishu.
The business is seasonal, but Sucdi says this year has been particularly encouraging, although numbers are still fairly low. Having five tourists a week is considered a success but she is confident that numbers will grow.
However, she says many visitors are still concerned about security.
Since the collapse of Somalia's central government in 1991, Mogadishu has endured decades of civil war, destruction and displacement. Much of the city centre was reduced to rubble, and basic services and infrastructure largely broke down.
But following the withdrawal of the Islamist militant group al-Shabab from most of the city in 2011, and the establishment of the federal government in 2012, Mogadishu has undergone a gradual transformation.
Returning members of the Somali diaspora, local entrepreneurs and investors helped fuel a construction boom, with new hotels, restaurants, businesses and residential developments reshaping the capital.
Today, Mogadishu is a growing commercial hub, although insecurity and the legacy of conflict remain part of everyday life.
About 10,000 tourists visited Somalia in 2024, a 50% increase on the previous year, according to the country's tourism department.
Many visitors ask about their safety before travelling and often encounter security checkpoints around the city.
But she says their experience on the ground is generally positive.
"What they heard from the news and everywhere else is not the same as what they see in the country," she says.
Although some question whether Mogadishu is safe enough for a young woman to be working as a tour guide, Sucdi is determined to continue.
She wants visitors to experience a Somalia that is rarely seen.
"I would want them to see the beautiful, welcoming side of Mogadishu, and not the side that they heard from the media, which is explosions and bombs," she says.
Somalia has Africa's longest mainland coastline, stretching more than 3,000km (1,860 miles) along the Indian Ocean and Gulf of Aden.
Its beaches and sand dunes sit alongside historic coastal cities such as Mogadishu, whose culture reflects centuries of Indian Ocean trade.
For some tourists, that contrast between the country's reputation and what they experience can be striking.

- Published

This is the image that one young Somali woman wants the world to have of her home city - in contrast to the one of suicide attacks and young men wielding AK-47s that many people currently associate with Somalia's capital.
Sucdi Abdul Fattah Abdul Khader is among a growing number of local guides taking visitors beyond the headlines to explore Mogadishu's beauty spots, historic sites and culture.
Her favourite spot is Jazeera beach, where visitors can enjoy the sea before heading to nearby sand dunes.
"It's one of the tourist attractions where we bring our guests. It's a nice place," says the 23-year-old.
The dunes, she adds, remind some visitors of the Sahara.
But her tours are about more than scenic views. She also takes visitors to the fish market, where they discover the variety of marine life available along Somalia's extensive coastline and to parts of the city that reflect its history as a busy Indian Ocean trading centre, with the influences of both its Ottoman and Italian former rulers.
Visitors can also sample Somali food, including camel meat, samosas and traditional tea.
Sucdi says many arrive in the city with expectations shaped by years of hearing about the insecurity.
"Mostly, they are surprised by how beautiful the country is and how welcoming people are," she says.
At the fish market, she says, visitors are particularly impressed by the variety of fish species.
Guiding tours runs in Sucdi's family. Her father worked in the profession for over three decades, taking journalists, photographers and visitors from different countries around Somalia.
He introduced her to the business nearly three years ago.

She now works alongside her father and a team of guides, building on his experience while using social media to reach a wider audience.

She is also considering producing content in English to reach audiences who do not speak Somali.

title: US carries out another round of ‘minor’ strikes on Iran, Trump says
content_c:
Donald Trump has said the US military on Friday carried out a new round of limited strikes on Iran, targeting an air defence system, describing the action as “minor.”
Iranian state media reported the sound of two explosions in the Suza area of Qeshm Island, which is in the strait of Hormuz, the crucial waterway for oil shipments that has been disrupted since the beginning of the US war on Iran in February.
In an exchange with reporters on Friday, Trump said “they built a little bit of an anti-aircraft device and we knocked it out in about 15 minutes, maybe five”.
The US military had previously reported carrying out what it described as “defensive” strikes on Monday, when explosions were heard on the islands of Qeshm and Hengam and in the nearby mainland area of Bandar Abbas.
Friday’s strikes are the first since Trump’s Republican party was dealt a stunning repudiation in Tuesday’s midterm elections in the US.
The electoral setback was stoked in part by voter dissatisfaction with Trump’s execution of the Iran war and elevated fuel prices – a byproduct of the war that has affected nearly every part of the global economy.
In the days since, Trump has vacillated between threatening to “destroy” Iran and suggesting a resolution to the war is near.
Differences with Iran about its nuclear program remain the thorniest issue and one that Trump insists must be resolved as part of any deal meant to end the war.
US Central Command, which oversees US military operations in the Middle East, announced in a post on X late Friday that the US was offering “a reward of up to $20m and possible relocation for information about Iran’s nuclear program, including its facilities, equipment, and associated personnel, such as those in the scientific community, or the movement of any of the above”.
The post included a link to the state department’s Rewards for Justice program.
Trump noted earlier Friday in an exchange with reporters that mediators’ discussions with Iran continue.
“We are talking to Iran. We have been,” said Trump.
A flurry of diplomatic phone calls in recent days between leaders in the Gulf and beyond has been aimed at easing tensions in the region. Concerns have mounted over the possibility that Trump could still order the US military to carry out new strikes against Iran.
US defense secretary Pete Hegseth spoke on Friday with his Qatari counterpart, Sheikh Saoud bin Abdulrahman Al Thani, about developments, according to the Qatari government. Qatar has been mediating between the US and Iran to end the war.
The Qatari government announced the call between the countries’ defence officials after confirming earlier that Trump and Qatar’s emir had a separate call to discuss efforts to de-escalate tensions.
The telephone call between Trump and Qatar’s Emir Sheikh Tamim bin Hamad al Thani focused on international efforts to end tensions, according to a statement from the Qatari ruler’s media office.
With the Associated Press

title: Zambia's civil service overhaul raises questions
content_c:
Zambia's opposition criticizes government restructuring and layoffs
November 6, 2026
Many people living in Zambia seek careers in the civil service because of the stability and security traditionally associated with government employment. But recent retirements, dismissals and restructuring exercises across several public institutions have unsettled that perception and sparked a national debate about the government's use of "national interest" provisions.
Among those affected is former public relations officer Godfrey Chilabi, whose departure from the Zambia Police Service was announced in October. Choosing not to publicly discuss the circumstances surrounding his exit, Chilabi simply told media that he had been retired in the national interest.
"Yes, I have been retired in national interest," Chilabi said. "I can't give any reason, but know I'm in retirement."
Chilabi's departure came amid a series of changes affecting public institutions in Zambia.
Charity Munganga, a Zambia Police Service deputy inspector general, was dismissed, and all staff members at the Zambia Medicines and Medical Supplies Agency were let go as part of a "reset" following a government audit.
Additionally, all directors in senior management at the Zambia Environmental Management Agency (ZEMA) were put on administrative leave to facilitate an institutional realignment exercise.
The affected ZEMA directors will be assessed for their competence, performance and suitability for their positions before a final decision is made on whether they will be reinstated or separated from the institution, according to an October 20 statement by the Green Economy and Environment Ministry cited by the news portal Mwebantu.
Zambia's public servants on edge
The issue moved to the center of public debate in October, when opposition lawmakers questioned the government in parliament over retirements and dismissals taking place across public institutions following Zambia's general election in August.
Governance and political commentator Andrew Nguvu told DW that retirements carried out in the national interest raise important questions about transparency, fairness and the protection of a professional public service.
"If at all, there are legitimate reasons for retiring any particular civil servant, then obviously the government should clearly explain," Nguvu said.
He said public institutions should operate according to established procedures and the law rather than political considerations that could undermine institutional independence.
Zambian law allows service commissions to retire established officers in the national interest under provisions governing public service employment. Previous governments have also used the measure. However, the current exercise has generated significant scrutiny because it is occurring alongside broader restructuring efforts affecting multiple institutions.
Opposition cries hypocrisy
Critics argue that the issue is particularly sensitive because Zambia's ruling United Party for National Development (UPND) previously opposed the use of retirements in the national interest while in opposition.
As a result, opposition lawmakers, led by Stephen Kampyongo, have criticized the measures, which they view as inconsistent with the ruling party's earlier position.
Kampyongo, speaking during Vice President's Question Time in the National Assembly on October 17, asked what assurances the government was giving public servants, who are "working in fear," and what measures were being taken to ensure that government workers retired in the national interest did not become destitute.
Government pushes back
Responding on behalf of the government, Vice President Mutale Nalumango rejected suggestions that the exercise amounted to a political purge and described it as part of a lawful process of institutional realignment.
Nalumango acknowledged the concerns surrounding the changes but defended the government's authority to make personnel adjustments within the public service framework.
"As provided for in section 39 of the Public Service Pensions Act, there are situations that arise and people fall by the way side," Nalumango told the parliament. "[It is] unfortunate that a life was lost, but maybe it is an issue that public servants/public service workers must brace themselves for."
Nalumango's comments have been cited by critics as evidence that additional changes could occur as the government continues to restructure public institutions.
The debate has been amplified by comments from UPND National Youth Chairperson Gilbert Liswaniso, who said governments naturally sought to work with people aligned with their vision.
"Every political party [that] comes to power has to flush out!" Liswaniso said. "[It] has to work with the people aligned with the vision of that political party!"
Critics say such statements reinforce concerns that political considerations may be influencing decisions within the public service.
The civil rights activist David Chishimba rejects the notion that perceived political affiliation should determine a person's future in government employment.
"The constitution, however, is very clear on this," Chishimba told DW. "It restricts public officers from participating in partisan politics while in office. This safeguards an impartial civil service. However, it does not prohibit private political belief or otherwise."
Chishimba said civil servants served the country rather than any political organization. "Civil servants serve Zambia," he said, "not a party, the president or a campaign."
Workers face uncertainty
Nguvu said the shift was deeply unsettling for public workers caught in the middle of the administrative realignments.
The measures come as the cost of living and household debt burdens increase in Zambia.
Nguvu said abrupt personnel changes could affect morale throughout the public service and leave workers uncertain about their professional future.
"This can weaken morale and help to destroy institutional memory," Nguvu said. "Most of these decisions lack clear explanations."
Nguvu said such concerns had become more acute when explanations for personnel decisions were not communicated clearly.
The reported dismissals have also raised concerns among civil society groups about due process and accountability.
Chishimba, who is also the president of the Zambia Council of Activists (ZACA), called for greater transparency from the authorities.
"ZACA respectfully calls on the government to publish the names and evidence of those facing dismissal, submit every case to due process, and allow the Civil Service Commission to assert its constitutional independence," Chishimba said

title: Kanarische Inseln melden vermehrte Flüchtlingsankünfte
content_c:
Gefährliche Migrationsroute Kanaren melden immer mehr Flüchtlingsankünfte
Spanien schlägt Alarm. Die Zahl der ankommenden Flüchtlinge auf El Hierro, einer kleinen kanarischen Insel, steigt seit Anfang November wieder stark an. Die Behörden warnen vor Ausnahmezuständen wie 2024.
Die spanische Seenotrettung und das Rote Kreuz sind im Dauereinsatz. Mehr als 3.200 Menschen erreichten in den ersten fünf Tagen des Monats die Kanarischen Inseln, darunter mehr als 300 Kinder und Jugendliche, einschließlich elf Babys.
Die meisten Flüchtlingsboote kamen auf El Hierro an, mit gerade mal 11.000 Einwohnern, eine der kleinsten Inseln der Inselgruppe. Von dort aus werden die Migranten in Hilfseinrichtungen auf andere Inseln und weiter auf das spanische Festland gebracht. Die Inselbehörden waren vor einer ähnlichen Überlastung wie 2024, als innerhalb eines Jahres mehr als 46.800 Menschen über den Atlantik Spanien erreichten.
Damals sorgte vor allem die Verteilung der Minderjährigen für politischen Streit. Die Atlantikroute gilt wegen der unberechenbaren Strömungen und der oft tagelangen Überfahrt als eine der gefährlichsten Migrationsrouten der Welt. Laut Vereinten Nationen galten im vergangenen Jahr mindestens 1.200 Menschen als vermisst, sie sind vermutlich ertrunken.
Fischer- und Schlauchboote zu gefährlich
Hilfsorganisationen berichten, dass Schlepperorganisationen neben den sogenannten Cayucos - offenen Fischerbooten aus Holz - auch immer öfter Schlauchboote einsetzen, teils mit doppelt so vielen Menschen an Bord wie für solche Boote vorgesehen. Da diese Boote niedriger und instabiler sind, können sie besonders leicht kentern.

title: Мерц зустрінеться з Мадяром у Берліні: серед тем — підтримка України
content_c:
Мерц зустрінеться з Мадяром у Берліні: серед тем — підтримка України
Переговори канцлера Німеччини та прем’єр-міністра Угорщини заплановані на 10 листопада.
Федеральний канцлер Німеччини Фрідріх Мерц прийме в Берліні прем’єр-міністра Угорщини Петера Мадяра. Однією з тем зустрічі стане подальша підтримка України.
Про це повідомила пресслужба федерального уряду ФРН.
За словами речника уряду Штефана Корнеліуса, сторони також обговорять європейські питання, оборону та економічне співробітництво.
Спочатку Мерц і Мадяр проведуть розмову віч-на-віч. Після цього заплановані переговори делегацій, робочий обід за участю окремих міністрів і спільна пресконференція.
Попередня зустріч лідерів у Берліні відбулася 2 червня, під час першого офіційного візиту Мадяра до Німеччини після вступу на посаду. Тоді вони також обговорювали підтримку України та євроатлантичну безпеку.
Нагадаємо, що раніше Фрідріх Мерц та Дональд Трамп провели телефонну розмову, у якій погодилися з необхідністю якнайшвидшого припинення війни в Україні за обов’язкового узгодження мирної угоди з НАТО.

title: "Шахтер" — "Динамо": онлайн-трансляция центрального матча УПЛ
content_c:
Поединок пройдет во Львове.
В воскресенье, 8 ноября, во Львове на стадионе "Арена Львов" в рамках 12-го тура украинской Премьер-лиги встретятся донецкий "Шахтер" и киевское "Динамо".
"Шахтер" — "Динамо": прогноз букмекеров.
После 11 сыгранных туров "Шахтер" идет на первом месте в турнирной таблице УПЛ, а "Динамо" с десятью сыгранными играми находится на третьем месте (22 очка).
Отметим, что "Шахтер" на неделе провел тяжелый поединок Лиги чемпионов против "Спортинга", проиграв минимально в Лондоне (0:1).
"Горняки" не смогут рассчитывать на своих травмированных бразильцев Педриньо и Кауана Элиаса, а "Динамо" сыграет без дисквалифицированных Михавко, Ярмоленко, Герреро и травмированного Буяльского.
Киевский клуб после увольнения Игоря Костюка и назначения Мацея Кендзерека выиграл два подряд поединка в УПЛ против "Кудровки" и "Кривбасса".
"Шахтер" и "Динамо" в октябре уже встречались в 1/8 финала Кубка Украины, и победу во Львове со счетом 3:0 одержали дончане.
На игре будет работать бригада арбитров во главе с 39-летним харьковчанином Дмитрием Панчишиным.

title: Зеленський анонсував кадрові рішення в ЗСУ
content_c:
Президент України Володимир Зеленський повідомив про підготовку кадрових рішень у Збройних силах України, не надавши деталей, але зазначивши, що вони узгоджені з головнокомандувачем ЗСУ Михайлом Драпатим.
"Ми готуємо рішення з Головнокомандувачем – кадрові рішення в Збройних Силах України. Я хочу подякувати усім, хто служить Україні!", – сказав Зеленський у вечірньому відеозверненні в п'ятницю.

title: This man refused life-saving treatment because of his religion - days later the rules changed
content_c:
This man refused life-saving treatment because of his religion - days later the rules changed
- Published
In August this year, 26-year-old Isaac Valdez had an epileptic seizure while browsing in his local library, causing him to convulse and strike his head against the ground.
He lost consciousness. Later, in hospital, it transpired Isaac had hit his head with such force it had led to a brain haemorrhage.
Treatment was seriously complicated by the fact that, as a Jehovah's Witness, Isaac carried a "No Blood" card, an indication that he would not accept treatment involving any form of blood transfusion because of his religious beliefs.
As a result, a procedure to drain fluid from Isaac's brain did not take place.
But his family, from Waxahachie, Texas, were encouraged by the fact that he regained consciousness and even started to talk again. He was able to confirm that he stood by his "no blood" beliefs.
The family's relief at his apparent improvement was short-lived. Isaac slipped into a coma and his condition worsened rapidly.
A neurosurgeon told Isaac's family the only way to save his life was an emergency operation, but that it was one that required blood transfusion.
His family took the decision to abide by Issac's wishes as a lifelong Witness not to accept such a procedure.
Isaac - who his twin brother Jacob Valdez describes as an intelligent man who loved volunteering and helping the elderly - died on 26 August 2026 when doctors turned off his life support.
Just 23 days later, the Jehovah's Witnesses' Governing Body announced a seismic change in teaching that would, in effect, have given Isaac the religious green light to have the life-saving treatment he had refused.
The change suddenly means the vast majority of medical procedures using donated blood are no longer prohibited to followers. Now, decisions on whether to accept such treatments are to be left to individuals.
Jacob, already dealing with the death of his twin, was angered at the Jehovah's Witnesses' leadership for not coming to their conclusion sooner. He told BBC News he believes Isaac could well still be alive if they had.
The original rule on blood transfusions dates back to 1945, towards the very end of a war during which the use of blood transfusions had been increasingly widespread. The leaders of Jehovah's Witnesses announced that their believers were not permitted to accept transfusions.
This was based on their interpretation of Bible verses from both the Old and New Testaments prohibiting the consumption of blood, including one from the Book of Acts that instructs believers to abstain from blood, from food offered to idols, and from things that had been strangled.
So, why has the Jehovah's Witnesses' Governing Body, based in New York state, now decided to change the rules, 81 years after introducing them?
It comes after years of pressure from both within and outside the faith, but that is not how leaders of the faith describe the decision.
"The change is basically the application of Bible principles to modern medicine and its methods," says the Jehovah's Witnesses international spokesperson, Paul Gillies, who described it as both a fresh look at scripture and at medical advances.
We meet Gillies at the Jehovah's Witnesses UK headquarters set in 85 acres of Essex countryside. It is a vast modern complex where hundreds of volunteer followers of the faith live and work without pay.
He insists the basic teaching has not changed and that the transfusion of whole blood is still prohibited. However, for decades, most transfusions have not used whole blood, instead using the specific components of blood that are needed by the patient.
The change is being justified by permitting the use of blood components, like plasma and red blood cells and platelets, in the huge numbers of medical procedures that were previously banned.
Gillies says the Bible references "abstaining from blood" but not "various components that could be extracted from blood".
He says the Governing Body felt it their duty to avoid scriptural "overreach" and only apply what was specifically described in the Bible.
But that explanation has stunned many and led them to ask if it was not a huge overreach 81 years ago to ban blood transfusions in the first place, when transfusions are not specifically mentioned in the bible.
Others are then also asking why it has taken so long to come to this landmark decision, given that transfusions that do not use whole blood have been the norm for decades.
These are questions Jacob asked as soon as the ban was lifted, just days after a memorial service for Isaac.
Jacob, who had already left the Jehovah's Witness faith he was brought up in, texted prominent figures from Isaac's congregation in Texas after Isaac's death. The messages are full of angst, and painful to read.
He asked them to consider "the part you played in encouraging so many people to sacrifice their life for something that was never God's will".
Most did not reply, but one "elder" responded saying he could not understand why Jacob was so angry and fixated on the policy shift.
This all further infuriated Jacob, who particularly wants the faith's decision-makers to be accountable for all the lives lost.
"I want to ask them if they could apologise directly, I would like not to have a deflected answer, just straightforward apology," he says.
It is extremely difficult to say how many Jehovah's Witnesses, among the estimated nine million followers of the faith worldwide, died each year having refused treatment involving blood transfusions. But research in one medical journal in 2016, The Obstetrical & Gynecological Survey, put the figure at around 1,100.
"We're sympathetic to their feelings, and if individuals have lost family members and are concerned about some of these questions, they deserve to be heard compassionately," says Gillies.
But there was little clarity about why the change did not come earlier.
"Why has it taken this time? Well, I guess because it takes time, it doesn't necessarily mean that there is some magic change that's taken place," says Gillies.
And when asked, Gillies deflects calls for the leadership to apologise, saying that many lives had, in fact, been saved because faithful Jehovah's Witnesses had not been exposed to blood contamination scandals.
He also insists that even after the new edict, some Jehovah's Witnesses could still decide they did not want to accept a transfusion, and that may have been the case even if the edict had come years ago.
Indeed, the BBC spoke with Alex Ball, 58, a Jehovah's Witness from West Sussex, who says in 2012 a doctor told him he would not survive the chemotherapy he needed to treat his blood cancer unless he also had a transfusion.
"I wanted to adhere as closely to the scriptures as possible when I was sick, and I think I did that well."
With help from what is called "a Jehovah's Witness Hospital Liaison Committee", Alex found an American consultant who could perform a treatment to boost Alex's blood cells without the need for any products from someone else. His UK consultant agreed to treat him using the new method and it worked.
More than a decade later, Alex says he would make the same decision again, despite the change in blood policy that would have permitted the transfusions he had been told he needed.
It is not just receiving blood which has been an issue.
Elisha Cummings, 50, a Jehovah's Witness from Trinidad and Tobago, was unable to donate blood to her aunt, who died, because of the rules.
They also cost her her marriage too, with her husband of 10 years leaving the faith and divorcing her after it came to light that he had had a blood transfusion as a child, something that was looked down upon in her Witness community.
"Since the blood policy change, I have not been myself," she says. "It left me in a sort of depressed mode."
"How many houses did I go to trying to convince people about the blood doctrine? And you're coming now and it's something totally different," Elisha says.
Elisha says her beliefs as a whole have been shaken, yet she feels reluctant to leave the faith, partly because it is what provides her with her community and she fears isolation.
In the past, those who disagreed with "blood doctrine" were ostracised or felt like they needed to leave the faith. Will they now be able to come back?
"Any individual that wants to come back to the faith is warmly welcomed," says Gillies, speaking of those who had left the faith because they had accepted a transfusion for themselves or a relative.
"If they would like to become one of Jehovah's Witnesses again and would like to speak to the elders, then they're very welcome to do so."

But there was little clarity about why the change did not come earlier.
"Why has it taken this time? Well, I guess because it takes time, it doesn't necessarily mean that there is some magic change that's taken place," says Gillies.
And when asked, Gillies deflects calls for the leadership to apologise, saying that many lives had, in fact, been saved because faithful Jehovah's Witnesses had not been exposed to blood contamination scandals.
He also insists that even after the new edict, some Jehovah's Witnesses could still decide they did not want to accept a transfusion, and that may have been the case even if the edict had come years ago.
Indeed, the BBC spoke with Alex Ball, 58, a Jehovah's Witness from West Sussex, who says in 2012 a doctor told him he would not survive the chemotherapy he needed to treat his blood cancer unless he also had a transfusion.
"I wanted to adhere as closely to the scriptures as possible when I was sick, and I think I did that well."
With help from what is called "a Jehovah's Witness Hospital Liaison Committee", Alex found an American consultant who could perform a treatment to boost Alex's blood cells without the need for any products from someone else. His UK consultant agreed to treat him using the new method and it worked.
More than a decade later, Alex says he would make the same decision again, despite the change in blood policy that would have permitted the transfusions he had been told he needed.
It is not just receiving blood which has been an issue.
Elisha Cummings, 50, a Jehovah's Witness from Trinidad and Tobago, was unable to donate blood to her aunt, who died, because of the rules.
They also cost her her marriage too, with her husband of 10 years leaving the faith and divorcing her after it came to light that he had had a blood transfusion as a child, something that was looked down upon in her Witness community.
"Since the blood policy change, I have not been myself," she says. "It left me in a sort of depressed mode."
"How many houses did I go to trying to convince people about the blood doctrine? And you're coming now and it's something totally different," Elisha says.
Elisha says her beliefs as a whole have been shaken, yet she feels reluctant to leave the faith, partly because it is what provides her with her community and she fears isolation.
In the past, those who disagreed with "blood doctrine" were ostracised or felt like they needed to leave the faith. Will they now be able to come back?
"Any individual that wants to come back to the faith is warmly welcomed," says Gillies, speaking of those who had left the faith because they had accepted a transfusion for themselves or a relative.
"If they would like to become one of Jehovah's Witnesses again and would like to speak to the elders, then they're very welcome to do so."

title: Russell Brand suspected to have attacked at least 10 other women
content_c:
Police are bracing themselves for more victims of Russell Brand to come forward, with at least 10 more women suspected of having been attacked by the disgraced star.
Brand, 51, will be sentenced on Monday to what is expected to be a lengthy jail sentence for rape and sexual assaults after he abused his fame to become a “predator” targeting women, and got away with it for years.
The fallout from Brand’s case saw the government pledge to examine calls to crack down on “rape myths” in trials.
The Guardian also understands that next week the Metropolitan police team that built the case against Brand will start sifting through reports and intelligence about other potential victims.
The Met commissioner, Sir Mark Rowley, said there could be “many more” victims, but declined to say how many, with some intelligence about further victims being third-hand and some further suspected victims reluctant to face the criminal justice system.
Sources say it is feared the number of further victims is at least in “double digits”, with 10 currently seen as a minimum.
The Met police said on Thursday that Brand was under investigation for two further rape allegations. Detectives have sent files to specialist rape prosecutors and are in discussions with them over the material.
Rowley said: “We’ve got two other victims who’ve come forward who want to tell their story, and so two rape cases we’re investigating. I wouldn’t be surprised if many, many more come forward, and we’re open to that.”
Rowley declined on LBC Radio to confirm the new allegations would reach “double figures”, and said: “I’m not going to guess on this, but we’ve seen in the past with high-profile individuals who are brought to justice that it does often bring out a flood of other cases. Let’s see where this one goes.”
Brand’s trial, which spanned claims of attacks from 1999 to 2009, saw women asked by the defence barrister why they had not screamed during attacks.
Since the end of the trial there has been a debate about rape myths. A No 10 source said the prime minister, Andy Burnham, believed calls from the victims’ commissioner, Claire Waxman, for a legal duty that would require judges to issue directions to juries on rape myths and misconceptions, should be examined.
A Ministry of Justice spokesperson said: “Rape myths have absolutely no place in our courts and victims should never feel as though they are the ones on trial.
“Judges are already able to give directions to counter rape myths … we will also carefully consider the victims’ commissioner’s proposals as we continue to strengthen protections for victims.”
Siobhan Blake, the Crown Prosecution Service (CPS) lead for rape and serious sexual offences, said: “The focus must be the actions of the perpetrator and not the behaviour of the victim.
“We know that there is no typical response to sexual assault and myths that victims should scream and fight back are outdated. Some people may freeze or feel unable to speak about it for months or even years, but this is not a barrier to justice.”
Brand now faces years of imprisonment and the growing prospect of a fresh trial over further allegations.
He was convicted on Thursday of raping a young fan at his luxury London townhouse in 2009, continuing despite her pleas for him to stop. He had picked her out of a crowd. He was also found guilty of sexually assaulting three women in separate incidents at a radio station, a recording studio and a bar.
Victims are expected to tell of the impact his crimes had on them in court on Monday.
Brand became an international star, acting in Hollywood films, and in latter years an online influencer, but was dogged by whispers and allegations about his danger to women. He was accused of treating women as a “disposable commodity” and a “means to an end” to satisfy his voracious sexual appetite.
The government says it is committed to reducing violence against women and girls by half.
Burnham told Times Radio: “It’s horrifying what Russell Brand has done. And I’d firstly like to praise the bravery of the women, the victims in the case, who’ve come forward and had the courage to speak out.
“But yes, the journalists too, who supported those who had been abused by Russell Brand. So all of them deserve our praise for having that courage to come forward.”
Later on the BBC, Burnham was asked about a statement of support for Brand in 2014 as the star faced media criticism, and said: “Well, over a decade ago, and all I can say is I had no idea of the full extent of what he was doing or what he went on to do. His crimes are horrific.”
Burnham told Times Radio he will look at making changes to rape trials so that they “do not leave the woman feeling like she is on trial”.
He said: “We need to constantly look at the way rape trials are conducted to make sure that they do not leave the woman feeling like she is on trial in court, as has been the experience of people in the past … we need to encourage more women to come forward to report rape.”
The comedian Katherine Ryan, who warned of a “predator” in the entertainment industry before Brand’s trial, said she felt relief at his conviction.
“They came forward despite Russell Brand having fame, power, money and a legion of fans ready to attack them,” she said.
“I will never be someone who, like, dances on graves. There has been some justice done today. There’s a level of relief, but there’s grief alongside relief.”
Bear Grylls, who baptised Brand when he converted to Christianity in 2024, said the star’s faith seemed genuine and added: “It is right that justice has now been served. I can’t imagine how hard this time has been for the victims, the heroes of the day.”
Brand was cleared of two further charges of rape and one allegation of attempted indecent assault.
Brand’s victims told how he “snapped” – changing from charming to nasty – as he raped and sexually assaulted them before gaslighting them into believing nothing was wrong.

title: What to know about the IIHF Women's Ice Hockey World Championship
content_c:
What to know about the IIHF Women's Ice Hockey World Championship
November 6, 2026
Why is the tournament being held in November?
Since its inception in 1990, the Women's Ice Hockey World Championship has almost always been held in the spring — apart from 2021 and 2022, when the COVID-19 pandemic saw it moved to the summer. This year, though, the tournament, being hosted by Denmark from November 6 to November 16, is being held in November for the first time. The idea is make it easier for all of the world's best players to participate. Since its inception in 2023, the North America-based Professional Women's Hockey League (PWHL), widely considered the world's best, has had to pause its season to allow players to take part in the Worlds. This is no longer necessary, as the PWHL's regular season doesn't open until December.
"This gives the women's game a unique selling point," International Ice Hockey Federation (IIHF) President Franz Reindl recently told the SID news agency. "Because the PWHL season begins after this, we can be certain that the very best players are participating."
How has the tournament format changed?
Previously, the teams were divided into a stronger group and a weaker group, with the idea being to avoid, as much as possible, lopsided scores. This is because women's hockey is not as balanced as the men's game, with Canada or the United States having won every tournament since its inception. Under the old system, all five teams in the stronger Group A advanced to the quarterfinals. Under the new format, four of the five teams advance from both groups. This also sees the two powerhouses, the USA and Canada in separate groups, meaning the marquee matchup can't occur early in the tournament.
Group A: USA, Czechia, Switzerland, Germany, Austria
Group B: Canada, Finland, Sweden, Japan, Denmark
Will Russia be competing at this tournament?
No. While the Court of Arbitration for Sport (CAS) ruled on October 30, 2026 — a week before the opening faceoff of the Women's Ice Hockey World Championship — that the IIHF must allow Russia back into its tournaments during the 2026-2027 season, it made no mention of this tournament. Under the CAS ruling though, the IIHF will be required to include Russia at the 2027 tournament in Quebec City.
Who are the contenders?
As noted above, either Canada or the United States has won every edition of this tournament – and indeed the two countries have split Olympic gold medals between them (Canada 5, USA 3) since the sport was introduced to the Winter Games in 1998. There is nothing to suggest that this is about to change in Herning and Esbjerg, although Canada enters the tournament with a vastly different roster from the one that won Olympic silver in Milano in February. Among those looking to break this North American domination are Finland, the only other team ever to have made it to a World Championship final and Switzerland, who took bronze in Milano.
Why are the USA and Canada not wearing their traditional uniforms?
The United States and Canada are having to play in generic kits provided by the International Ice Hockey Federation's official supplier due to an ongoing commercial rights dispute. The Canadian federation, Hockey Canada, said in a statement on Wednesday that its players would be wearing jerseys designed by True Hockey instead of their Bauer jerseys featuring the national team logo. USA Hockey has confirmed that its players too will be wearing jerseys without its national emblem.
"While we have yet to see the jersey Canada will be playing in on Friday, our team remains focused on the tournament and representing our country proudly on and off the ice,” Hockey Canada said.
description: As ice hockey's governing body continues to wrangle over how to respond to a CAS order to reinstate Russia to international play, the top women's tournament gets underway in Denmark without Russia.

title: EU-Staatsanwaltschaft ermittelt nach Zugunglück in Spanien
content_c:
Möglicher Subventionsbetrug EU-Staatsanwaltschaft ermittelt nach Zugunglück
Nach dem schweren Zugunglück in Spanien mit 69 Toten ermittelt die EU-Staatsanwaltschaft wegen möglichen Subventionsbetrugs. Im Fokus stehen Gelder für die Bahnsicherheit. Bereits nach einem Unglück im Januar gab es Ermittlungen.
Neun Tage nach dem schweren Zugunglück auf der Hochgeschwindigkeitsstrecke zwischen Madrid und Sevilla ermittelt die Europäische Staatsanwaltschaft wegen möglichen Betrugs mit EU-Fördergeldern. Spanische Ermittler sichteten im Auftrag der Behörde Unterlagen beim staatlichen Schienennetzbetreiber Adif, der Eisenbahnsicherheitsagentur und dem Rechnungshof.
Im Mittelpunkt stehen EU-Mittel, die für die Modernisierung der Sicherheits-, Signal- und Kommunikationssysteme auf der in Spanien meistbefahrenen Hochgeschwindigkeitsstrecke vorgesehen waren. Die Ermittler prüfen, ob es bei deren Verwendung Unregelmäßigkeiten gab.
69 Tote bei Zugunglück im Oktober
Ende Oktober waren bei Urda südlich von Madrid zwei Züge zusammengestoßen. 69 Menschen kamen ums Leben. Nach bisherigen Erkenntnissen war das automatische Zugsicherungssystem ausgefallen. Zudem könnten fehlerhafte Anweisungen aus der Leitstelle zu dem Unglück beigetragen haben.
Bereits im Januar waren bei einer Kollision zweier Hochgeschwindigkeitszüge auf derselben Strecke nahe Adamuz in Andalusien 46 Menschen gestorben. Als wahrscheinliche Ursache gilt ein Schienenbruch. Auch nach diesem Unglück leitete die EU-Staatsanwaltschaft Ermittlungen wegen möglichen Subventionsbetrugs ein. Damals ging es um Fördermittel für die Erneuerung der Gleise.

content_c:
У Ростові спалахнула пожежа біля заводу "Алмаз": що відомо
Exilenova+ повідомляє про масштабне займання в районі підприємства російського оборонно-промислового комплексу.
У російському Ростові повідомляють про масштабну пожежу в районі заводу «Алмаз». Про це пише Telegram-канал Exilenova+.
